translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 280
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 280

sentences.zh: 【後晉紀一】 柔兆涒灘，一年。

translations.literal: [Later Jin Records 1] From Rouzhao through Yousi, one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin Records 1 — from rouzhao through yousi, one year in total.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝上之上天福元年（

translations.literal: Gaozu the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuous Emperor of Filial Piety, Upper Part One, First Year of Tianfu (
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuous Emperor of Filial Piety, Part One, First Year of Tianfu (

sentences.zh: 丙申，公元九三六年）

translations.literal: Bingshen, the year 936 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingshen, AD 936)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，吳徐知誥始建大元帥府，以幕職分判吏、戶、禮、兵、刑、工部及鹽鐵。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Xu Zhigao of Wu first established the Grand Marshal's headquarters, with staff offices separately administering the ministries of Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Justice, and Works, as well as Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Xu Zhigao of Wu established a Grand Marshal's headquarters for the first time, assigning staff officers to oversee the six ministries and the Salt and Iron Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 丁未，唐主立子重美為雍王。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Tang emperor installed his son Chongmei as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the Tang emperor named his son Chongmei Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，唐主以千春節置酒，晉國長公主上壽畢，辭歸晉陽。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Tang emperor held a banquet for the Qianchun festival; when the Princess of Jin had finished offering birthday felicitations, she took leave to return to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the Tang emperor gave a feast for the Qianchun festival. After the Princess of Jin had presented her birthday wishes, she asked leave to return to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝醉，曰：「何不且留？

translations.literal: The emperor, drunk, said: "Why not stay awhile?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in his cups, said, "Why not stay a while?

sentences.zh: 遽歸，欲與石郎反邪！」

translations.literal: You hurry home — do you mean to rebel with Master Shi!
translations.idiomatic: You rush off home — are you plotting rebellion with that Shi fellow!

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭聞之，益懼。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang heard of this, he grew all the more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang heard this, his fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙午，以翰林學士、禮部侍郎馬胤孫為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingwu, Ma Yinsun, Hanlin academician and vice minister of Rites, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingwu, Ma Yinsun, Hanlin academician and vice minister of Rites, was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 胤孫性謹儒，中書事多凝滯，又罕接賓客，時人目為「三不開」，謂口、印、門也。

translations.literal: Yinsun was by nature cautious and scholarly; Secretariat affairs were often held up, and he rarely received guests. People of the time dubbed him the "Three Not Open" — meaning mouth, seal, and door.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsun was cautious and bookish by nature; business at the Secretariat often stalled, and he seldom received visitors. Contemporaries called him the "Three Not Open" — his mouth, his seal, and his door.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭盡收其貨之在洛陽及諸道者歸晉陽，託言以助軍費，人皆知其有異志。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang gathered all his goods in Luoyang and along the various transport circuits back to Jinyang, claiming this was to help military expenses; everyone knew he harbored ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang recalled all his property from Luoyang and the transport circuits to Jinyang, saying it was to fund the army, but everyone knew he had rebellion in mind.

sentences.zh: 唐主夜與近臣從容語曰：「石郎於朕至親，無可疑者；

translations.literal: At night the Tang emperor spoke at ease with close ministers, saying: "Master Shi is extremely close to me; there is nothing to suspect;
translations.idiomatic: One night the Tang emperor spoke casually with his close advisers: "Master Shi is as close to me as kin; there is no reason to doubt him;

sentences.zh: 但流言不息，萬一失歡，何以解之？」

translations.literal: but rumors never cease. If by any chance affection should be lost, how could that be remedied?"
translations.idiomatic: yet the rumors never stop. If we should fall out, how could that be set right?"

sentences.zh: 皆不對。

translations.literal: No one answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one replied.

sentences.zh: 端明殿學士、給事中李崧退謂同僚呂琦曰：「吾輩受恩深厚，豈得自同眾人，一概觀望邪！

translations.literal: Li Song, academician of the Duanming Hall and supervising secretary, withdrew and said to his colleague Lü Qi: "We have received deep favor; how can we be like the crowd and watch from the sidelines!
translations.idiomatic: Li Song, academician of the Duanming Hall and supervising secretary, withdrew and told his colleague Lü Qi, "We owe the emperor a deep debt of gratitude. How can we stand aside with the rest and merely watch!

sentences.zh: 計將安出？」

translations.literal: What plan shall we devise?"
translations.idiomatic: What shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「河東若有異謀，必結契丹為援。

translations.literal: Qi said: "If Hedong has rebellious designs, it will surely ally with the Khitan as support.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "If Hedong plots rebellion, it will surely seek Khitan aid.

sentences.zh: 契丹母以贊華在中國，屢求和親，但求萴剌等未獲，故和未成耳。

translations.literal: The Khitan empress dowager, because Zanhua was in China, repeatedly sought a marriage alliance, but because Wanla and others had not been returned, peace was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan empress dowager had often sought a marriage alliance because Prince Zanhua was held in China, but peace had failed because Wanla and the other captives had not been returned.

sentences.zh: 今誠歸萴刺等與之和，歲以禮幣約直十餘萬緡遺之，彼必歡然承命。

translations.literal: If we now truly return Wanla and the others and make peace with them, sending yearly gifts worth a little over one hundred thousand strings of cash, they will surely gladly accept.
translations.idiomatic: If we now return Wanla and the rest and make peace, sending annual gifts worth a little over one hundred thousand strings of cash, they will gladly agree.

sentences.zh: 如此，則河東雖欲陸梁，無能為矣。」

translations.literal: In this way, even if Hedong wished to act unruly, it could accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Then even if Hedong wished to rebel, it could do nothing."

sentences.zh: 崧曰：「此吾志也。

translations.literal: Song said: "This is my intent as well.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "That is exactly what I had in mind.

sentences.zh: 然錢穀皆出三司，宜更與張相謀之。」

translations.literal: Yet funds and grain all come from the Three Commissions; we ought to consult further with Chancellor Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: But funds and grain all pass through the Three Commissions, so we should discuss this further with Chancellor Zhang."

sentences.zh: 遂告張延朗，延朗曰：「如學士計，不惟可以制河東，亦省邊費之什九，計無便於此者。

translations.literal: They then told Zhang Yanlang. Yanlang said: "As the academician plans, this would not only restrain Hedong but also save nine-tenths of frontier expenses; no policy could be more advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: They then told Zhang Yanlang, who said, "As you propose, this would not only check Hedong but save nine-tenths of frontier costs. No plan could be better.

sentences.zh: 若主上聽從，但責辦於老夫，請於軍財之外捃拾以供之，他夕，二人密言於帝，帝大喜，稱其忠，二人私草《遺契丹書》以俟命。

translations.literal: If His Majesty approves, charge only this old man to arrange it — I shall scrape together supplies beyond military funds. Another evening the two men spoke privately to the emperor; he was greatly pleased and praised their loyalty. The two privately drafted a "Letter to the Khitan" to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: If His Majesty agrees, leave it to me — I will scrape together the funds beyond the military budget. That night the two men spoke privately to the emperor, who was delighted and praised their loyalty. They privately drafted a letter to the Khitan to await his command.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝以其謀告樞密直學士薛文遇，文遇對曰：「以天子之尊，屈身奉夷狄，不亦辱乎！

translations.literal: After some time the emperor told his plan to the direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Xue Wenyü. Wenyü replied: "For one of the Son of Heaven's dignity to humble himself before barbarians — is that not shameful!
translations.idiomatic: After a time the emperor told his plan to Xue Wenyü, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Wenyü replied, "For the Son of Heaven to humble himself before barbarians — is that not shameful!

sentences.zh: 又，虜若循故事求尚公主，何以拒之？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the barbarians follow precedent and seek a princess in marriage, how could that be refused?"
translations.idiomatic: And if the Khitan follow custom and ask for an imperial princess, how could we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 因誦戎昱《昭君詩》曰：「安危托婦人。」

translations.literal: He then recited Rong Yu's "Zhaojun Poem": "Safety and peril are entrusted to a woman."
translations.idiomatic: He then quoted Rong Yu's poem on Wang Zhaojun: "Safety and peril are entrusted to a woman."

sentences.zh: 帝意遂變。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind then changed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind turned.

sentences.zh: 一日，急召崧、琦至後樓，盛怒，責之曰：「卿輩皆知古今，欲佐人主致太平；

translations.literal: One day he urgently summoned Song and Qi to the rear pavilion, furiously rebuking them: "You all know antiquity and the present and wish to help the ruler bring peace;
translations.idiomatic: One day he urgently summoned Song and Qi to the rear pavilion and rebuked them in a rage: "You know history and wish to help your sovereign bring peace;

sentences.zh: 今乃為謀如是！

translations.literal: yet now you devise plans like this!
translations.idiomatic: yet now you propose this!

sentences.zh: 朕一女尚乳臭，卿欲棄之沙漠邪？

translations.literal: My daughter is still in swaddling clothes — do you wish to abandon her in the desert?
translations.idiomatic: My daughter still smells of milk — do you mean to cast her into the desert?

sentences.zh: 且欲以養士之財輸之虜庭，其意安在？」

translations.literal: And you wish to send funds meant to support the army to the barbarian court — what is your intent?"
translations.idiomatic: And you would send the funds meant to support our troops to the barbarian court — what do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 二人懼，汗流浹背，曰：「臣等志在竭愚以報國，非為虜計也，願陛下察之。」

translations.literal: The two were afraid, sweat soaking their backs, and said: "We mean only to exhaust our wit in service to the state, not to plan for the barbarians; we beg Your Majesty to see this."
translations.idiomatic: The two were terrified, sweat soaking their backs. They said, "We meant only to serve the state with all our wit, not to scheme for the Khitan. We beg Your Majesty to see that."

sentences.zh: 拜謝無數，帝詬責不已。

translations.literal: They bowed and apologized without end, but the emperor reviled them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed and apologized again and again, but the emperor kept berating them.

sentences.zh: 呂琦氣竭，拜少止，帝曰：「呂琦強項，肯視朕為人主邪！」

translations.literal: Lü Qi, his strength spent, paused slightly in his bowing. The emperor said: "Lü Qi is stiff-necked — does he refuse to regard me as his sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Qi, exhausted, paused in his bowing. The emperor said, "Lü Qi is stiff-necked — does he refuse to treat me as his sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「臣等為謀不臧，願陛下治其罪，多拜可為！」

translations.literal: Qi said: "We devised an unworthy plan; we wish Your Majesty to punish our crime — more bowing is of no use!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Our plan was ill-advised. Punish us as you will — more bowing will not help!"

sentences.zh: 帝怒稍解，止其拜，各賜卮酒罷之，自是群臣不敢復言和親之策。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger eased somewhat; he stopped their bowing and gave each a cup of wine before dismissing them. From then on the ministers did not dare speak again of a marriage-alliance policy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased. He stopped their bowing, gave each a cup of wine, and dismissed them. After that no minister dared raise the marriage-alliance plan again.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以琦為御史中丞，蓋疏之也。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Qi was appointed vice censor-in-chief — evidently to distance him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Qi was made vice censor-in-chief — clearly a move to keep him at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥以其子副都統景通為太尉、副元帥，都統判官宋齊丘、行軍司馬徐玠為元帥府左、右司馬。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao of Wu appointed his son, deputy commander-in-chief Jingtong, Grand Marshal and deputy commander-in-chief; the commander-in-chief's aide Song Qiqiu and marching marshal Xu Jie became left and right marshals of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao of Wu made his son Jingtong, deputy commander-in-chief, Grand Marshal and deputy commander-in-chief, and named Song Qiqiu, the commander-in-chief's aide, and Xu Jie, marching marshal, left and right marshals of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 閩主昶改元通文，立賢妃李氏為皇后，尊皇太后曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: The lord of Min, Chang, changed the era name to Tongwen, installed the Worthy Consort Lady Li as empress, and honored the empress dowager as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Min, Chang, changed the era name to Tongwen, made the Worthy Consort Lady Li empress, and elevated the empress dowager to grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 靜江節度使、同平章事馬希杲有善政，監軍裴仁照譖之於楚王希範，言其收眾心，希範疑之。

translations.literal: Ma Xigao, military governor of Jingjiang and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, had good governance; the army supervisor Pei Renzhao slandered him to the King of Chu, Xifan, saying he was winning popular hearts, and Xifan grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xigao, military governor of Jingjiang and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, governed well, but the army supervisor Pei Renzhao slandered him to King Xifan of Chu, saying he was winning the people's loyalty, and Xifan grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，漢將孫德威侵蒙、桂二州，希範命其弟武安節度副使希廣權知軍府事，自將步騎五千如桂州。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the Han general Sun Dewei invaded the two prefectures of Meng and Gui. Xifan ordered his younger brother, deputy military commissioner of Wu'an, Xiguang, to act as provisional commander of the headquarters, and himself led five thousand infantry and cavalry toward Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Han general Sun Dewei invaded Meng and Gui prefectures. Xifan left his brother Xiguang, deputy commissioner of Wu'an, in charge of headquarters affairs and led five thousand foot and horse troops to Gui Prefecture himself.

sentences.zh: 希杲懼，其母華夫人逆希範於全義嶺，謝曰：「希杲為治無狀，致寇戎入境，煩殿下親涉險阻，皆妾之罪也。

translations.literal: Xigao was afraid. His mother, Lady Hua, went to meet Xifan at Quanyi Ridge and apologized: "Xigao has governed without discipline, bringing enemy raiders across the border and troubling Your Highness to brave hardship in person — all is this concubine's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Xigao was afraid. His mother, Lady Hua, met Xifan at Quanyi Ridge and apologized: "Xigao has governed badly, letting the enemy cross the border and forcing Your Highness to brave danger in person. The fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 願削封邑，灑掃夜庭，以贖希杲罪。」

translations.literal: I wish to reduce my fief and sweep the night court to atone for Xigao's crime."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to forfeit my fief and sweep the night court to atone for Xigao's offense."

sentences.zh: 希範曰：「吾久不見希杲，聞其治行尤異，故來省之，無它也。」

translations.literal: Xifan said: "I have long not seen Xigao and heard his governance was especially outstanding, so I came to visit him — nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: Xifan said, "I have not seen Xigao in a long time and heard his governance was exceptional, so I came to visit him — nothing more."

sentences.zh: 漢兵自蒙州引去，徙希杲知朗州。

translations.literal: The Han troops withdrew from Meng Prefecture, and Xigao was transferred to govern Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Han troops withdrew from Meng Prefecture, and Xigao was transferred to Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高從誨遣使奉箋於徐知誥，勸即帝位。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui sent an envoy to present a memorial to Xu Zhigao, urging him to take the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui sent an envoy with a memorial to Xu Zhigao, urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，石敬瑭欲嘗唐王之意，累表自陳贏疾，乞解兵柄，移他鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi Jingtang wished to test the Tang ruler's intent and repeatedly memorialized, claiming illness and begging to relinquish military authority and transfer to another command.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shi Jingtang wished to test the Tang emperor's mind and repeatedly memorialized that he was ill, asking to give up his command and transfer elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 帝與執政議從其請，移鎮鄆州。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed with the chief ministers acceding to his request and transferring him to the Yanzhou command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed the request with his chief ministers and agreed to move him to the Yanzhou command.

sentences.zh: 房暠、李崧、呂琦等皆力諫，以為不可，帝猶豫久之。

translations.literal: Fang Hao, Li Song, Lü Qi, and others all strongly remonstrated that this could not be done; the emperor hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hao, Li Song, Lü Qi, and others all strongly urged against it, and the emperor hesitated for a long time.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅夜，李崧請急在外，薛文遇獨直，帝與之議河東事，文遇曰：「諺有之：『當道築室，三年不成。』

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the night of gengyin, Li Song requested urgent audience outside; Xue Wenyü alone was on duty. The emperor discussed Hedong affairs with him. Wenyü said: "As the proverb has it: 'Build a house in the road — three years and it is not finished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the night of gengyin, Li Song sought an urgent audience outside, while Xue Wenyü alone was on duty. The emperor discussed Hedong with him. Wenyü said, "As the proverb goes, 'Build a house in the road and three years will not finish it.

sentences.zh: 茲事斷自聖志；

translations.literal: This matter must be decided by the sacred will;
translations.idiomatic: This matter must be decided by Your Majesty alone;

sentences.zh: 群臣各為身謀，安肯盡言！

translations.literal: the ministers each plot for themselves — how would they speak their whole mind!
translations.idiomatic: the ministers each plot for themselves. How would they speak their whole mind!

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，河東移亦反，不移亦反，在旦暮耳，不若先事圖之。」

translations.literal: In this subject's view, if Hedong is transferred it will rebel; if not transferred it will rebel — it is only a matter of morning or evening. Better to take the initiative."
translations.idiomatic: In my view, if Hedong is transferred it will rebel; if it is not transferred it will rebel all the same. It is only a matter of time. Better to strike first."

sentences.zh: 先是，術者言國家今年應得賢佐，出奇謀，定天下。

translations.literal: Earlier, diviners had said the state this year should obtain a worthy assistant who would devise a singular stratagem and settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, diviners had said the state would gain a worthy aide this year who would devise a singular stratagem and settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝意文遇當之，聞其言，大喜，曰：「卿言殊豁吾意，成敗吾決行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor thought Wenyü was the man. Hearing his words, he was greatly pleased and said: "Your words greatly clarify my intent; success or failure I shall decide and carry out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Wenyü was that man. Hearing him, he was delighted and said, "Your words clarify my mind completely. Success or failure — I will decide and act."

sentences.zh: 即為除目，付學士院使草制。

translations.literal: He immediately drafted appointment orders and handed them to the Hanlin Academy to draft the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately drafted appointment orders and sent them to the Hanlin Academy to draft the edicts.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以敬瑭為天平節度使，以馬軍都指揮使、河陽節度使宋審虔為河東節度使。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Jingtang was made military governor of Tianping; Song Shenqian, commander of the horse army and military governor of Heyang, was made military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Jingtang was made military governor of Tianping, and Song Shenqian, commander of the horse army and military governor of Heyang, was made military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 製出，兩班聞呼敬瑭名，相顧失色。

translations.literal: When the edicts were issued, the two ranks of officials, hearing Jingtang's name called, looked at one another in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: When the edicts were issued, the court officials, hearing Jingtang's name called, looked at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以建雄節使張敬達為西北蕃漢馬步都部署，趣敬瑭之鄆州。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Zhang Jingda, commissioner of Jianxiong, was made overall commander of Khitan and Han horse and foot in the northwest, to hurry Jingtang to the Yanzhou command.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zhang Jingda, commissioner of Jianxiong, was made overall commander of Khitan and Han forces in the northwest and ordered to hurry Jingtang to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭疑懼，謀於將佐曰：「吾之再來河東也，主上面許終身不除代；

translations.literal: Jingtang was suspicious and afraid and consulted his generals and aides: "When I came again to Hedong, His Majesty face to face promised I would never be replaced in my lifetime;
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang was suspicious and afraid and consulted his officers: "When I returned to Hedong, His Majesty promised face to face that I would never be replaced in my lifetime;

sentences.zh: 今忽有是命，得非如今年千春節與公主所言乎？

translations.literal: now suddenly there is this order — could it not be like what was said at this year's Qianchun festival with the princess?
translations.idiomatic: now suddenly comes this order. Could it not be what was said at this year's Qianchun festival with the princess?

sentences.zh: 我不興亂，朝廷發之，安能束手死於道路乎！

translations.literal: If I do not raise rebellion and the court provokes me, how can I die bound hand and foot on the road!
translations.idiomatic: If I do not rebel and the court provokes me, how can I die bound hand and foot on the road!

sentences.zh: 今且發表稱疾以觀其意，若其寬我，我當事之；

translations.literal: For now let us send a memorial claiming illness to observe their intent; if they are lenient with me, I shall serve them;
translations.idiomatic: For now let us send a memorial claiming illness to test their intent. If they are lenient, I will obey;

sentences.zh: 若加兵於我，我則改圖耳。」

translations.literal: if they send troops against me, I shall change my plan."
translations.idiomatic: if they send troops against me, I will change my plan."

sentences.zh: 幕僚段希堯極言拒之，敬瑭以其樸直，不責也。

translations.literal: The staff officer Duan Xiyao strongly urged refusal; Jingtang, considering him simple and upright, did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer Duan Xiyao strongly urged refusal, but Jingtang, considering him simple and honest, did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 節度使判官華陰趙瑩勸敬瑭赴鄆州；

translations.literal: The military governor's aide Zhao Ying of Huayin urged Jingtang to proceed to Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The military governor's aide Zhao Ying of Huayin urged Jingtang to go to Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 觀察判官平遙薛融曰：「融書生，不習軍旅。」

translations.literal: the surveillance commissioner aide Xue Rong of Pingyao said: "Rong is a scholar and does not understand military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: the surveillance commissioner aide Xue Rong of Pingyao said, "I am a scholar and know nothing of military affairs."

sentences.zh: 都押牙劉知遠曰：「明公久將兵，得士卒心；

translations.literal: The chief military aide Liu Zhiyuan said: "Your Excellency has long commanded troops and won the soldiers' hearts;
translations.idiomatic: The chief military aide Liu Zhiyuan said, "Your Excellency has long commanded troops and holds the soldiers' hearts;

sentences.zh: 今據形勝之地，士馬精強，若稱兵傳檄，帝業可成，奈何以一紙制書自投虎口乎！」

translations.literal: now you hold terrain of strategic advantage, with elite troops and horses. If you raise arms and issue a proclamation, an imperial enterprise can be achieved — how can you cast yourself into a tiger's maw for a single written order!"
translations.idiomatic: you now hold strategic ground with elite troops and horses. Raise arms and issue a proclamation and an imperial enterprise can be achieved. How can you throw yourself into a tiger's maw for a single written order!"

sentences.zh: 掌書記洛陽桑維翰曰：「主上初即位，明公入朝，主上豈不知蛟龍不可縱之深淵邪？

translations.literal: The secretarial aide Sang Weihan of Luoyang said: "When His Majesty first took the throne, Your Excellency entered court — did His Majesty not know a flood dragon cannot be released into the deep abyss?
translations.idiomatic: The secretarial aide Sang Weihan of Luoyang said, "When His Majesty first took the throne, Your Excellency came to court. Did he not know a flood dragon cannot be released into the deep?

sentences.zh: 然卒以河東復授公，引乃天意假公以利器。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Hedong was given back to you — this is Heaven's intent lending you a sharp weapon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he gave you Hedong again. This is Heaven lending you a sharp weapon.

sentences.zh: 明宗遺愛在人，主上以庶孽代之，群情不附。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong's lingering affection remains among the people; the present ruler replaced him as a lesser-born son — popular sentiment does not attach.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong's affection still lives in the people's hearts. The present ruler is a lesser-born son who replaced him, and popular sentiment does not follow.

sentences.zh: 公明宗之愛婿，今主上以反逆見待，此非首謝可免，但力為自全之計。

translations.literal: You are Mingzong's beloved son-in-law; now the ruler treats you as a rebel — this cannot be escaped by bowing your head in apology; you must only strive for a plan of self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: You are Mingzong's beloved son-in-law, yet the ruler now treats you as a rebel. Bowing your head will not save you. You must strive only to preserve yourself.

sentences.zh: 契丹主素與明宗約為兄弟，今部落近在雲、應，公誠能推心屈節事之，萬一有急，朝呼夕至，何患無成。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler long ago pledged brotherhood with Mingzong; now their tribes are near Yun and Ying. If you can truly open your heart and humble yourself to serve them, should emergency arise they will come at a morning's call by evening — what fear of failure?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler long pledged brotherhood with Mingzong, and their tribes are now near Yun and Ying. If you can truly open your heart and humble yourself to serve them, they will come at a morning's call by evening if need arises. What fear of failure?"

sentences.zh: 敬瑭意遂決。

translations.literal: Jingtang's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷疑敬瑭，以羽林將軍寶鼎楊彥詢為北京副留守，敬瑭將舉事，亦以情告之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court suspected Jingtang and appointed Yang Yanxun of Baoding, general of the Imperial Guard, deputy defender of the Northern Capital. When Jingtang was about to act, he also told him his plans.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had suspected Jingtang and appointed Yang Yanxun of Baoding, a general of the Imperial Guard, deputy defender of the Northern Capital. When Jingtang was about to rebel, he told Yanxun his plans as well.

sentences.zh: 彥詢曰：「不知河東兵糧幾何，能敵朝廷乎？」

translations.literal: Yanxun said: "I do not know how much grain and troops Hedong has — can it match the court?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun said, "I do not know how much grain and troops Hedong has. Can it match the court?"

sentences.zh: 左右請殺彥詢，敬瑭曰：「惟副使一人我自保之，汝輩勿言也。」

translations.literal: Those at his side asked to kill Yanxun. Jingtang said: "I alone will guarantee the deputy defender's safety — you must not speak of this."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants asked to kill Yanxun. Jingtang said, "I alone will guarantee the deputy defender's safety. Say nothing of this."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，昭義節度使皇甫立奏敬瑭反。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Huangfu Li, military governor of Zhaoyi, memorialized that Jingtang had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Huangfu Li, military governor of Zhaoyi, reported that Jingtang had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭表：「帝，養子，不應承祀，請傳位許王。」

translations.literal: Jingtang memorialized: "The emperor is an adopted son and ought not inherit the sacrifices; I beg the throne be passed to the Prince of Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang memorialized: "The emperor is an adopted son and ought not inherit the throne. I beg that the succession pass to the Prince of Xu."

sentences.zh: 帝手裂其表抵地，以詔答之曰：「卿於鄂王固非疏遠，衛州之事，天下皆知；

translations.literal: The emperor tore the memorial by hand and cast it to the ground, replying by edict: "You are surely not distant from Prince E; the affair at Weizhou — the whole realm knows it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tore the memorial by hand and flung it to the ground, replying by edict: "You are surely not distant from Prince E. The affair at Weizhou — the whole realm knows it;

sentences.zh: 許王之言，何人肯信！」

translations.literal: words about the Prince of Xu — who would believe them!"
translations.idiomatic: as for words about the Prince of Xu — who would believe them!"

sentences.zh: 壬寅，制削奪敬瑭官爵。

translations.literal: On renyin, an edict stripped Jingtang of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, an edict stripped Jingtang of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以張敬達兼太原四面排陳使，河陽節度使張彥琪為馬步軍都指揮使，以安國節度使安審琦為馬軍都指揮使，以保義節度使相裡金為步軍都指揮使，以右監門上將軍武廷翰為壕寨使。

translations.literal: On yisi, Zhang Jingda was additionally made deployment commander on all four sides of Taiyuan; Zhang Yanqi, military governor of Heyang, was made overall commander of horse and foot; An Shenqi, military governor of Anguo, was made commander of the horse army; Xiangli Jin, military governor of Baoyi, was made commander of the foot army; Wu Tinghan, right gate guard general, was made trench-camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Zhang Jingda was also made deployment commander on all four sides of Taiyuan; Zhang Yanqi, military governor of Heyang, was made overall commander of horse and foot; An Shenqi, military governor of Anguo, was made commander of the horse army; Xiangli Jin, military governor of Baoyi, was made commander of the foot army; and Wu Tinghan, right gate guard general, was made trench-camp commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以張敬達為太原四面兵馬都部署，以義武節度使楊光遠為副部署。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Zhang Jingda was made overall deployment commander of horse and foot on all four sides of Taiyuan; Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Yiwu, was made deputy deployment commander.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Zhang Jingda was made overall deployment commander of forces on all four sides of Taiyuan, and Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Yiwu, was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 丁未，又以張敬達知太原行府事，以前彰武節度使高行周為太原四面招撫、排陳等使。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Zhang Jingda was further made acting administrator of the Taiyuan field headquarters; Gao Xingzhou, former military governor of Zhangwu, was made commissioner for pacification and deployment on all four sides of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Zhang Jingda was also put in charge of the Taiyuan field headquarters, and Gao Xingzhou, former military governor of Zhangwu, was made commissioner for pacification and deployment on all four sides of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光遠既行，定州軍亂，牙將千乘方太討平之。

translations.literal: After Guangyuan had set out, the army at Ding Prefecture mutinied; the military aide Fang Tai of Qiansheng suppressed it.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangyuan had set out, the army at Ding Prefecture mutinied, and the military aide Fang Tai of Qiansheng put it down.

sentences.zh: 張敬達將後三萬營於晉安鄉，戊申，敬達奏西北先鋒馬軍都指揮使安審信叛奔晉陽。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda led thirty thousand rear troops and encamped at Jin'an township. On wushen, Jingda memorialized that An Shenxin, commander of the northwest vanguard horse army, had rebelled and fled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda led thirty thousand rear troops and encamped at Jin'an township. On wushen, Jingda reported that An Shenxin, commander of the northwest vanguard horse army, had defected to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 審信，金全之弟子也，敬瑭與之有舊。

translations.literal: Shenxin was a nephew of An Jinquan; Jingtang had old ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxin was a nephew of An Jinquan and had old ties with Jingtang.

sentences.zh: 先是，雄義都指揮使馬邑安元信將所部六百餘人戍代州，代州刺史張朗善遇之，元信密說朗曰：「吾觀石令公長者，舉事必成；

translations.literal: Earlier, An Yuanxin of Mayi, commander of the Xiongyi command, garrisoned Dai Prefecture with more than six hundred of his troops. The prefect of Dai, Zhang Lang, treated him well. Yuanxin secretly urged Lang: "I observe that Commander Shi is a man of stature — if he acts, he will surely succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, An Yuanxin of Mayi, commander of the Xiongyi command, garrisoned Dai Prefecture with more than six hundred men. The prefect Zhang Lang treated him well. Yuanxin secretly urged Lang, "Commander Shi is a man of stature. If he acts, he will surely succeed;

sentences.zh: 公何不潛遣人通意，可以自全。」

translations.literal: why do you not secretly send someone to convey your intent — you can thereby preserve yourself."
translations.idiomatic: why not secretly send someone to convey your intent? You can save yourself."

sentences.zh: 朗不從，由是互相猜忌。

translations.literal: Lang did not follow this, and from this mutual suspicion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Lang refused, and from then on they mistrusted each other.

sentences.zh: 元信謀殺朗，不克，帥其眾奔審信，審信遂帥麾下數百騎與元信掠百井奔晉陽。

translations.literal: Yuanxin plotted to kill Lang but failed, then led his troops to join Shenxin. Shenxin then led several hundred horsemen under his command with Yuanxin, raiding Baijing and fleeing to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxin plotted to kill Lang but failed, then led his men to Shenxin. Shenxin then led several hundred horsemen with Yuanxin, raided Baijing, and fled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭謂元信曰：「汝見何利害，捨強而歸弱？」

translations.literal: Jingtang said to Yuanxin: "What advantage or harm did you see, that you abandoned the strong and returned to the weak?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang said to Yuanxin, "What did you see in the balance of advantage and harm, that you abandoned the strong and came to the weak?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「元信非知星識氣，顧以人事決之耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Yuanxin does not read stars or discern qi — I judged only by human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I do not read the stars or discern omens. I judged by human affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王所以御天下，莫重於信。

translations.literal: Of all means by which emperors and kings govern the realm, none is weightier than trust.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the means by which emperors govern the realm, none is weightier than trust.

sentences.zh: 今主上失大信於令公，親而貴者且不自保，況疏賤乎！

translations.literal: Now the sovereign has grievously broken faith with Your Excellency; even those close and noble cannot yet preserve themselves — how much less the distant and lowly!
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign has now lost all faith with Your Excellency. Even those who are close and exalted cannot save themselves — how much less those who are distant and humble!

sentences.zh: 其亡可翹足而待，何強之有！」

translations.literal: Their destruction can be awaited with crossed legs — what strength is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Their fall can be waited for at leisure. Where is their strength?"

sentences.zh: 敬瑭悅，委以軍事。

translations.literal: Jingtang was pleased and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang was pleased and put him in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 振武西北巡檢使安重榮戍代北，帥步騎五百奔晉陽。

translations.literal: An Chongrong, Zhenwu Northwest patrol commissioner, was garrisoning the northern Dai region; he led five hundred infantry and cavalry in flight to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: An Chongrong, the Zhenwu Northwest patrol commissioner, was stationed in northern Dai when he led five hundred infantry and horsemen in flight to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 重榮，朔州人也。

translations.literal: Chongrong was a native of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong was from Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 以宋審虔為寧國節度使、充待衛馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Song Shenqian was made military governor of Ningguo and appointed commander of the palace horse army.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenqian was appointed military governor of Ningguo and commander of the palace horse army.

sentences.zh: 天雄節度使劉延皓恃後族之勢，驕縱，奪人財產，減將士給賜，宴飲無度。

translations.literal: Liu Yanhao, military governor of Tianxiong, relied on the power of the empress's clan. He was arrogant and unrestrained, seized people's property, reduced the soldiers' allowances, and feasted and drank without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanhao, military governor of Tianxiong, traded on the empress's family connections. He was arrogant and wild, seized people's property, cut the soldiers' pay, and feasted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 捧聖都虞候張令昭因眾心怨怒，謀以魏博應河東，癸丑未明，帥眾攻牙城，克之；

translations.literal: Zhang Lingzhao, chief military adjutant of Pingsheng, taking advantage of widespread resentment, plotted to have Weibo respond to Hedong. Before dawn on guichou he led troops to attack the headquarters compound and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingzhao, chief military adjutant of Pingsheng, seizing on the troops' anger, plotted to have Weibo side with Hedong. Before dawn on guichou he led his men against the headquarters and captured it;

sentences.zh: 延皓脫身走，亂兵大掠。

translations.literal: Yanhao escaped with his life and fled; the mutinous troops looted on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhao escaped and fled, while the mutinous soldiers plundered the city.

sentences.zh: 令昭奏：「延皓失於撫御，以致軍亂；

translations.literal: Lingzhao memorialized: "Yanhao failed in comforting and controlling the troops, thus causing the army to mutiny;
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhao memorialized, "Yanhao failed to control his troops, which led to the mutiny;

sentences.zh: 臣以撫安士卒，權領軍府，乞賜旌節！」

translations.literal: Your subject has pacified the soldiers and temporarily holds command of the army headquarters; I beg that insignia of office be granted!"
translations.idiomatic: I have pacified the soldiers and temporarily assumed command of the headquarters. I beg to be granted the commission of office!"

sentences.zh: 延皓至洛陽，唐主怒，命遠貶；

translations.literal: When Yanhao reached Luoyang, the Tang emperor was angry and ordered him banished to a distant post;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhao reached Luoyang, the Tang emperor was furious and ordered him exiled to a distant post;

sentences.zh: 皇后為之請，六月，庚申，止削延皓官爵，歸私第。

translations.literal: The empress pleaded on his behalf. In the sixth month, on gengshen, he was only stripped of rank and office and sent to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: The empress interceded for him. In the sixth month, on gengshen, the emperor merely stripped Yanhao of his rank and office and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，吳太保、同平章事徐景遷以疾罷，以其弟景遂代為門下侍郎、參政事。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Xu Jingqian of Wu, Grand Guardian and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was removed due to illness; his younger brother Jing-sui was made vice director of the Secretariat and participant in government affairs in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Xu Jingqian of Wu, Grand Guardian and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, resigned due to illness. His younger brother Jing-sui replaced him as vice director of the Secretariat and participant in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，唐主以張令昭為右千牛衛將軍、權知天雄軍計事。

translations.literal: On guihai, the Tang emperor appointed Zhang Lingzhao General of the Right Thousand Bull Guard and provisional overseer of Tianxiong army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Tang emperor made Zhang Lingzhao General of the Right Thousand Bull Guard and provisional overseer of Tianxiong army affairs.

sentences.zh: 令昭以調發未集，且受新命。

translations.literal: Lingzhao, on the grounds that mobilization was not yet complete, also accepted the new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Citing incomplete mobilization, Lingzhao also accepted the new appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔徙齊州防禦使，令昭托以士卒所留，實俟河東之成敗。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered his transfer to defender of Qizhou. Lingzhao pleaded that the soldiers were holding him back, but in truth he was waiting to see how Hedong would fare.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon ordered his transfer to defender of Qizhou. Lingzhao claimed the soldiers would not let him go, but in truth he was waiting to see how the Hedong campaign would turn out.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣使諭之，令昭殺使者。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor sent envoys to instruct him, and Lingzhao killed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor sent envoys to order him to comply, and Lingzhao had them killed.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以宣武節度使兼中書令范延光為天雄四面行營招討使、知魏博行府事，以張敬達充太原四面招討使，以楊光遠為副使。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Fan Yanguang, military governor of Xuanwu and concurrently chief minister, was made commander of the Tianxiong four-sided campaign headquarters and overseer of Weibo field headquarters affairs; Zhang Jingda was made commander of the four-sided Taiyuan campaign; Yang Guangyuan was made deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Fan Yanguang, military governor of Xuanwu and chief minister, was made commander of the Tianxiong campaign and given charge of Weibo headquarters affairs. Zhang Jingda was made Taiyuan campaign commander, with Yang Guangyuan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以西京留守李周為天雄軍四面行營副招討使。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Li Zhou, defender of the Western Capital, was made deputy commander of the Tianxiong four-sided campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Li Zhou, defender of the Western Capital, was made deputy commander of the Tianxiong campaign.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭之子右衛上將軍重殷、皇城副使重裔聞敬瑭舉兵，匿於民間井中。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang's sons — Chong Yin, senior general of the Right Guard, and Chong Yi, deputy commissioner of the Imperial City — upon hearing that Jingtang had raised troops, hid in a civilian well.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that Jingtang had risen in arms, Shi Jingtang's sons Chong Yin, senior general of the Right Guard, and Chong Yi, deputy commissioner of the Imperial City, hid in a civilian's well.

sentences.zh: 弟沂州都指揮使敬德殺其妻女而逃，尋捕得，死獄中，從弟彰聖都指揮使敬威自殺。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jingde, commander of Yizhou, killed his wife and daughter and fled; he was soon captured and died in prison. His younger cousin Jingwei, commander of Pingsheng, committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jingde, commander of Yizhou, killed his wife and daughter and fled, but was soon captured and died in prison. His cousin Jingwei, commander of Pingsheng, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊子，獲重殷、重裔，誅之，並族所匿之家。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on wuzi, Chong Yin and Chong Yi were captured and executed, and the household that had hidden them was extirpated to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on wuzi, Chong Yin and Chong Yi were captured and executed, and the family that had sheltered them was wiped out to the clan.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，楚王希範自桂州北還。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the King of Chu, Xifan, returned north from Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, King Xifan of Chu returned north from Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雲州步軍指揮使桑遷奏應州節度使尹暉逐雲州節度使沙彥珣，收其兵應河東。

translations.literal: Sang Qian, commander of the Yunzhou infantry, reported that Yin Hui, military governor of Yingzhou, had driven out Sha Yanxun, military governor of Yunzhou, taken over his troops, and responded to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Qian, commander of the Yunzhou infantry, reported that Yin Hui, military governor of Yingzhou, had driven out Sha Yanxun, military governor of Yunzhou, seized his troops, and declared for Hedong.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，彥珣表遷謀叛應河東，引兵圍子城。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Yanxun memorialized that Qian was plotting rebellion in support of Hedong and led troops to besiege the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Yanxun memorialized that Qian was plotting to rebel for Hedong and led troops to besiege the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 彥昫犯圍走出西山，據雷公口，明日，收兵入城擊亂兵，遷敗走，軍城復安。

translations.literal: Yanxun broke through the siege and fled west into the mountains, holding Leigongkou. The next day he gathered troops, entered the city, and attacked the mutinous soldiers. Qian was defeated and fled, and the military city was restored to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxun broke through the siege and escaped to the western hills, holding Leigongkou. The next day he rallied his troops, entered the city, and attacked the mutineers. Qian was defeated and fled, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 是日，尹暉執遷送洛陽，斬之。

translations.literal: That same day Yin Hui seized Qian and sent him to Luoyang, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yin Hui seized Qian, sent him to Luoyang, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 丁未，范延光拔魏州，斬張令昭。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Fan Yanguang captured Weizhou and executed Zhang Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Fan Yanguang took Weizhou and executed Zhang Lingzhao.

sentences.zh: 詔悉誅其黨七指揮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all seven commanders of his faction be executed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all seven conspirators among the commanders be executed.

sentences.zh: 張敬達發懷州彰聖軍戍虎北口，其指揮使張萬迪將五百騎奔河東，丙辰，詔盡誅其家。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda dispatched the Pingsheng army from Huaizhou to garrison Hubekou. Its commander Zhang Wandi led five hundred horsemen in flight to Hedong. On bingchen an edict ordered their families entirely executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda sent the Pingsheng army from Huaizhou to garrison Hubekou. Its commander Zhang Wandi led five hundred horsemen in flight to Hedong. On bingchen an edict ordered all their families executed.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭遣間使求救於契丹，令桑維翰草表稱臣於契丹主，且請以父禮事之，約事捷之日，割盧龍一道及雁門關以北諸州與之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang sent secret envoys to beg aid from the Khitan and had Sang Weihan draft a memorial declaring himself subject to the Khitan ruler, furthermore requesting to serve him with the rites due a father, with the agreement that upon success the entire Lulong circuit and all prefectures north of Yanmen Pass would be ceded to them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang sent secret envoys to beg the Khitan for aid and had Sang Weihan draft a memorial declaring himself the Khitan ruler's subject and asking to treat him as a father, promising that upon success he would cede the entire Lulong circuit and all prefectures north of Yanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 劉知遠諫曰：「稱臣可矣，以父事之太過。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiyuan remonstrated, saying: "Declaring oneself subject is acceptable; serving him with fatherly rites goes too far.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan advised, "Declaring yourself his subject is one thing, but treating him as a father goes too far.

sentences.zh: 厚以金帛賂之，自足致其兵，不必許以土田，恐異日大為中國之患，悔之無及。」

translations.literal: Bribing them richly with gold and silk would suffice to bring their troops; there is no need to promise them land. I fear that one day this will become a great calamity for China, and it will be too late to regret it."
translations.idiomatic: A generous bribe of gold and silk would be enough to bring their armies. There is no need to promise them territory. I fear this will become a grave disaster for China one day, and then it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 敬瑭不從。

translations.literal: Jingtang did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang refused.

sentences.zh: 表至契丹，契丹主大喜，白其母曰：「兒比夢石郎遣使來，今果然，此天意也。」

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the Khitan, the Khitan ruler was greatly delighted and told his mother: "Your son lately dreamed that Master Shi would send envoys; now it has indeed come true — this is Heaven's will."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the Khitan, the Khitan ruler was overjoyed and told his mother, "I dreamed that Master Shi would send envoys, and now it has come true. This is Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 乃為復書，許俟仲秋傾國赴援。

translations.literal: He then wrote a reply, promising that by mid-autumn he would mobilize the whole nation to come to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a reply promising to mobilize the entire nation for aid by mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 八月，己未，以范延光為天雄節度使，李周為宣武節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiwei, Fan Yanguang was made military governor of Tianxiong, and Li Zhou was made military governor of Xuanwu and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiwei, Fan Yanguang was appointed military governor of Tianxiong, and Li Zhou was made military governor of Xuanwu and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，應州言契丹三千騎攻城。

translations.literal: On guihai, Yingzhou reported that three thousand Khitan horsemen were attacking the city.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Yingzhou reported that three thousand Khitan cavalry were attacking the city.

sentences.zh: 張敬達築長圍以攻晉陽。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda built a long encirclement to attack Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda built siege lines to attack Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭以劉知遠為馬步都指揮使，安重榮、張萬迪降兵皆隸焉。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang made Liu Zhiyuan overall commander of horse and foot; the surrendered troops of An Chongrong and Zhang Wandi were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang made Liu Zhiyuan overall commander of horse and foot, placing An Chongrong's and Zhang Wandi's surrendered troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 知遠用法無私，撫之如一，由是人無貳心。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan applied the law without favoritism and treated them all alike, and so the men had no divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan enforced the law impartially and treated all alike, so none of the men wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭親乘城，坐臥矢石下，知遠曰：「觀敬達輩高壘深塹，欲為持久之計，無他奇策，不足慮也。

translations.literal: Jingtang personally mounted the walls and sat and slept beneath arrows and stones. Zhiyuan said: "Looking at Jingda and his sort — high ramparts and deep ditches, intending a long-term plan — they have no other clever stratagem and are not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang personally manned the walls, eating and sleeping under arrow and stone fire. Zhiyuan said, "Jingda and his men have raised high ramparts and dug deep trenches, planning a war of attrition. They have no other stratagem and are not worth worrying about.

sentences.zh: 願明公四出間使，經略外事。

translations.literal: I hope Your Excellency will dispatch secret envoys in all directions to manage external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Excellency to send secret envoys in all directions to manage affairs abroad.

sentences.zh: 守城至易，知遠獨能辦之。」

translations.literal: Defending the city is extremely easy; Zhiyuan alone can manage it."
translations.idiomatic: Defending the city is the easy part — I alone can handle that."

sentences.zh: 敬瑭執知遠手，撫其背而賞之。

translations.literal: Jingtang took Zhiyuan's hand, patted his back, and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang took Zhiyuan's hand, clapped his back, and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以成德節度使董溫琪為東北面副招討使，以佐盧龍節度使趙德鈞。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Dong Wenqi, military governor of Chengde, was made deputy commander of the northeast campaign to assist Zhao Dejun, military governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Dong Wenqi, military governor of Chengde, was made deputy northeast campaign commander to assist Zhao Dejun, military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 唐主使端明殿學士呂琦至河東行營犒軍，楊光遠謂琦曰：「願附奏陛下，幸寬宵旰。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor sent Lu Qi, academician of the Duanming Hall, to the Hedong campaign headquarters to reward the troops. Yang Guangyuan said to Qi: "I wish to add a report for His Majesty: I hope he may ease his toil late into the night.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor sent Lu Qi of the Duanming Hall to the Hedong campaign headquarters to reward the troops. Yang Guangyuan told Qi, "Please convey to His Majesty my hope that he may rest easier at night.

sentences.zh: 賊若無援，旦夕當平；

translations.literal: If the rebels have no aid, they will be pacified within days;
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels receive no aid, they will fall within days;

sentences.zh: 若引契丹，當縱之令入，可一戰破也。」

translations.literal: If they bring in the Khitan, we should let them enter and can destroy them in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: If they bring in the Khitan, we should let them in and break them in one battle."

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝聞契丹許石敬瑭以仲秋赴援，屢督張敬達急攻晉陽，不能下。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that the Khitan had promised Shi Jingtang aid by mid-autumn and repeatedly pressed Zhang Jingda to press the attack on Jinyang, but the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that the Khitan had promised Shi Jingtang aid by mid-autumn, he repeatedly urged Zhang Jingda to press the attack on Jinyang, but the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 每有營構，多值風雨，長圍夏為水潦所壞，竟不能合，晉陽城中日窘，糧儲浸乏。

translations.literal: Whenever construction was undertaken, storms often intervened; in summer the long encirclement was damaged by floodwaters and could not be closed after all. Inside Jinyang city the situation grew daily more desperate, and grain stores gradually ran short.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever work began on the siege lines, storms intervened. In summer floods broke the encirclement, and it could never be fully closed. Inside Jinyang the situation grew daily more desperate, and supplies steadily dwindled.

sentences.zh: 九月，契丹主將五萬騎，號三十萬，自揚武谷而南，旌旗不絕五十餘里。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Khitan ruler led fifty thousand horsemen, proclaiming three hundred thousand, southward from Yangwu Valley; banners and flags stretched unbroken for more than fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Khitan ruler led fifty thousand horsemen south from Yangwu Valley, claiming three hundred thousand. Their banners and flags stretched unbroken for more than fifty li.

sentences.zh: 代州刺史張朗、忻州刺史丁審琦嬰城自守，虜騎過城下，亦不誘脅。

translations.literal: Zhang Lang, prefect of Daizhou, and Ding Shenqi, prefect of Xinzhou, closed their cities and held them. When barbarian horsemen passed below the walls, they did not entice or coerce them either.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang, prefect of Daizhou, and Ding Shenqi, prefect of Xinzhou, shut their cities and defended them. When Khitan horsemen passed beneath the walls, they neither coaxed nor threatened them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 審琦，洺州人也。

translations.literal: Shenqi was a native of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was from Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，契丹主至晉陽，陳於汾北之虎北口。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Khitan ruler reached Jinyang and deployed at Hubekou north of the Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the Khitan ruler reached Jinyang and formed his line at Hubekou on the north bank of the Fen.

sentences.zh: 先遣人謂敬瑭曰：「吾欲今日即破賊可乎？」

translations.literal: He first sent someone to say to Jingtang: "Do you wish me to break the rebels today at once?"
translations.idiomatic: He first sent word to Jingtang: "Shall I break the enemy today?"

sentences.zh: 敬瑭遣人馳告曰：「南軍甚厚，不可輕，請俟明日議戰未晚也。」

translations.literal: Jingtang sent a messenger in haste to report: "The southern army is very strong; it must not be taken lightly. Please wait until tomorrow to discuss battle — that will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang sent a hurried reply: "The southern army is very strong and must not be taken lightly. Please wait until tomorrow to discuss battle — that will be soon enough."

sentences.zh: 使者未至，契丹已與唐騎將高行周、符彥卿合戰，敬瑭乃遣劉知遠出兵助之。

translations.literal: Before the messenger arrived, the Khitan had already joined battle with the Tang cavalry generals Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing, and Jingtang then sent Liu Zhiyuan with troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Before the messenger arrived, the Khitan had already clashed with the Tang cavalry generals Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing. Jingtang then sent Liu Zhiyuan with troops to aid them.

sentences.zh: 張敬達、楊光遠、安審琦以步兵陳於城西北山下，契丹遣輕騎三千，不被甲，直犯其陳。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda, Yang Guangyuan, and An Shenqi deployed infantry in formation on the hills northwest of the city. The Khitan sent three thousand light horsemen, wearing no armor, to charge directly at their formation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda, Yang Guangyuan, and An Shenqi drew up their infantry on the hills northwest of the city. The Khitan sent three thousand light horsemen without armor to charge straight at their line.

sentences.zh: 唐兵見其贏，爭逐之，至汾曲，契丹涉水而去。

translations.literal: The Tang troops, seeing them weak, vied to pursue. Reaching the bend of the Fen, the Khitan crossed the water and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang troops, seeing how weak they looked, raced to pursue them. At the bend of the Fen the Khitan crossed the river and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 唐兵循岸而進，契丹伏兵自東北起，沖唐兵斷而為二，涉兵在北都多為契丹所殺，騎兵在南者引歸晉陷寨。

translations.literal: The Tang troops advanced along the bank. Khitan ambush troops rose from the northeast, charged the Tang army, and cut it in two. The infantry who had crossed to the north were mostly killed by the Khitan; the cavalry in the south withdrew to Jinxian fort.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang troops pressed along the bank. Khitan ambushers rose from the northeast, smashed into the Tang line, and cut it in two. Most of the infantry north of the river were slaughtered by the Khitan; the cavalry in the south retreated to Jinxian fort.

sentences.zh: 契丹縱兵乘之，唐兵大敗，步兵死者近萬人，騎兵獨全。

translations.literal: The Khitan unleashed their troops to exploit the advantage; the Tang army was routed. Nearly ten thousand infantry died; only the cavalry escaped intact.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pressed the advantage and the Tang army was routed. Nearly ten thousand infantry died; only the cavalry escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 敬達等收餘眾保晉安，契丹亦引兵歸虎北口。

translations.literal: Jingda and the others gathered the survivors and held Jin'an. The Khitan also withdrew their troops to Hubekou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda gathered the survivors and held Jin'an. The Khitan withdrew to Hubekou.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭得唐降兵千餘人，劉知遠勸敬瑭盡殺之。

translations.literal: Jingtang received more than a thousand Tang surrendered troops. Liu Zhiyuan urged Jingtang to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang took more than a thousand Tang surrendered troops. Liu Zhiyuan urged Jingtang to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 是夕，敬瑭出北門見契丹主，契丹主執敬瑭手，恨相見之晚。

translations.literal: That evening Jingtang went out the north gate to meet the Khitan ruler. The Khitan ruler took Jingtang's hand and lamented that they had met so late.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Jingtang went out the north gate to meet the Khitan ruler, who took his hand and regretted they had not met sooner.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭問曰：「皇帝遠來，士馬疲倦，遽與唐戰而大勝，何也？」

translations.literal: Jingtang asked: "Your Majesty came from afar; your troops and horses were weary, yet you rushed into battle with the Tang and won a great victory — how was this?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang asked, "Your Majesty came from afar with weary troops and horses, yet you rushed into battle with the Tang and won a great victory. How was that?"

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「始吾自北來，謂唐必斷雁門諸路，伏兵險要，則吾不可得進矣。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "When I first came from the north, I thought the Tang would certainly block the routes through Yanmen, with ambush troops at perilous passes — then I could not have advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said, "When I first came from the north, I expected the Tang to block the Yanmen routes and lay ambushes at the passes, which would have stopped me cold.

sentences.zh: 使人偵視，皆無之。

translations.literal: I sent men to reconnoiter — there were none.
translations.idiomatic: I sent scouts to look — and found nothing.

sentences.zh: 吾是以長驅深入，知大事必濟也。

translations.literal: Therefore I drove deep in a long advance and knew the great enterprise must succeed.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I drove deep into their territory, knowing the great enterprise would succeed.

sentences.zh: 兵既相接，我氣方銳，彼氣方沮，若不乘此急擊之，曠日持久，則勝負未可知矣。

translations.literal: Once the armies had joined, our spirit was still keen and theirs was already dampened. If we did not seize this moment to attack urgently, and the contest dragged on for days, then victory or defeat would have been uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, our spirit was high and theirs was already broken. If I had not struck hard at that moment, a prolonged fight would have made the outcome uncertain.

sentences.zh: 此吾所以亟戰而勝，不可以勞逸常理論也。」

translations.literal: This is why I fought urgently and won — one cannot judge it by the ordinary logic of exertion and rest."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I fought at once and won. You cannot judge it by the ordinary rules of rest and fatigue."

sentences.zh: 敬瑭甚歎伏。

translations.literal: Jingtang greatly admired and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，敬瑭引兵會契丹圍晉安寨，置營於晉安之南，長百餘里，厚五十里，多設鈴索吠犬，人跬步不能過。

translations.literal: On renyin, Jingtang led troops to join the Khitan in besieging Jin'an fort. They set up camps south of Jin'an, more than a hundred li long and fifty li deep, with many bells, ropes, and barking dogs — a man could not pass even a short step.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Jingtang joined the Khitan in besieging Jin'an fort. They encamped south of Jin'an in a block more than a hundred li long and fifty li deep, strung with bells and guard dogs — a man could not take a single step without being caught.

sentences.zh: 敬達等士卒猶五萬人，馬萬匹，四顧無所之。

translations.literal: Jingda and his men still had fifty thousand troops and ten thousand horses, but they looked in every direction and had nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda still had fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses, but they looked in every direction and saw nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，敬達遣使告敗於唐，自是聲問不復通。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Jingda sent envoys to report defeat to the Tang. From then on communications ceased.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Jingda sent envoys to report his defeat to the Tang court. After that, all contact was lost.

sentences.zh: 唐王大懼，遣彰聖都指揮使符彥饒將洛陽步騎兵屯河陽，詔天雄節度使兼中書令范延光將魏州二萬由青山趣榆次，盧龍節度使、東北面招討使兼中書令北平王趙德鈞將幽州兵由悄孤出契丹軍後，耀州防禦使潘環糾合西路戍兵由晉、絳兩乳嶺出慈、隰、共救晉安寨。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor was greatly afraid. He dispatched Fu Yanrao, commander of Pingsheng, to lead Luoyang infantry and cavalry to garrison Heyang. He ordered Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong and concurrently chief minister, to lead twenty thousand from Weizhou via Qingshan toward Yuci; Zhao Dejun, military governor of Lulong, commander of the northeast campaign and concurrently chief minister, Prince of Beiping, to lead Youzhou troops via Qiaogu to emerge behind the Khitan army; and Pan Huan, defender of Yaozhou, to muster western-route garrison troops via the two Rufeng passes of Jin and Jiang to come out through Ci, Xi, and Gong to rescue Jin'an fort together.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor was terrified. He sent Fu Yanrao, commander of Pingsheng, with Luoyang infantry and cavalry to garrison Heyang. He ordered Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong and chief minister, to lead twenty thousand men from Weizhou through Qingshan toward Yuci; Zhao Dejun, military governor of Lulong, northeast campaign commander, chief minister, and Prince of Beiping, to lead Youzhou troops through Qiaogu to strike behind the Khitan army; and Pan Huan, defender of Yaozhou, to gather western garrison troops through the Rufeng passes of Jin and Jiang to advance through Ci, Xi, and Gong and relieve Jin'an fort together.

sentences.zh: 契丹主移帳於柳林，游騎過石會關，不見唐兵。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler moved his headquarters to Liulin. His scouting horsemen passed Shihui Pass and saw no Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler moved his camp to Liulin. His scouts passed Shihui Pass and saw no Tang troops.

sentences.zh: 丁未，唐主下詔親征。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Tang emperor issued an edict that he would personally campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the Tang emperor issued an edict declaring a personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 雍王重美曰：「陛下目疾未平，未可遠涉風沙；

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Chongmei said: "Your Majesty's eye ailment is not yet healed; you must not travel far into wind and sand;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yong Chongmei said, "Your Majesty's eye ailment is not yet healed. You must not travel far into the northern wastes;

sentences.zh: 臣雖童稚，願代陛下北行。」

translations.literal: Your subject, though young, is willing to go north in Your Majesty's stead."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am still young, I am willing to go north in Your Majesty's place."

sentences.zh: 帝意本不欲行，聞之頗悅。

translations.literal: The emperor had in truth not wished to go, and on hearing this was rather pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never wanted to go, and was rather pleased to hear this.

sentences.zh: 張延朗、劉延皓及宣徽南院使劉延朗皆勸帝行，帝不得已，戊申，發洛陽，謂盧文紀曰：「朕雅聞卿有相業，故排眾議首用卿，今禍難如此，卿嘉謀皆安在乎？」

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, and Liu Yanlang, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Imperial Household, all urged the emperor to go. The emperor had no choice. On wushen he set out from Luoyang and said to Lu Wenji: "I long heard that you had the talent of a chief minister, and so I set aside the crowd's opinions and used you first — yet now calamity is thus; where have all your excellent plans gone?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, and Liu Yanlang, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Imperial Household, all urged the emperor to go. He had no choice. On wushen he set out from Luoyang and said to Lu Wenji, "I had always heard you had the makings of a chief minister, and so I chose you over all objections — yet now disaster has come. Where are all your fine plans?"

sentences.zh: 文紀但拜謝，不能對。

translations.literal: Wenji only bowed in apology and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji could only bow in apology and had no answer.

sentences.zh: 己酉，遣劉延朗監侍衛步軍都指揮使符彥饒軍赴潞州，為大軍後援。

translations.literal: On jiyou, he dispatched Liu Yanlang to oversee the army of Fu Yanrao, commander of the palace foot army, to proceed to Luzhou as rear support for the main army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, he sent Liu Yanlang to oversee Fu Yanrao, commander of the palace foot army, on his march to Luzhou as rear support for the main force.

sentences.zh: 諸軍自鳳翔推戴以來，驕悍不為用，彥饒恐其為亂，不敢束之以法。

translations.literal: Since the armies had been raised through the Fengxiang acclamation, they had been arrogant and fierce and would not submit to use. Yanrao feared they would mutiny and dared not restrain them with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Fengxiang acclamation, the armies had been arrogant and uncontrollable. Yanrao feared they would mutiny and dared not discipline them.

sentences.zh: 帝至河陽，心憚北行，召宰相、樞密使議進取方略，盧文紀希帝旨，言「國家根本、太半在河南。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Heyang, his heart feared going north. He summoned the chief ministers and military affairs commissioners to discuss strategy for advancing. Lu Wenji, reading the emperor's intent, said: "The state's foundation — more than half of it — lies south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Heyang, he feared going north. He summoned the chief ministers and military affairs commissioners to discuss strategy. Reading the emperor's mind, Lu Wenji said, "More than half of the state's foundation lies south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 胡兵倏來忽往，不能久留；

translations.literal: Barbarian troops come suddenly and go suddenly; they cannot stay long;
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian horsemen come and go quickly and cannot stay long;

sentences.zh: 晉安大寨甚固，況已發三道兵救之。

translations.literal: The great encampment at Jin'an is very solid; moreover, three columns of troops have already been dispatched to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The great fort at Jin'an is strong, and three relief columns have already been dispatched.

sentences.zh: 河陽天下津要，車駕宜留此鎮撫南北，且遣近臣往督戰，苟不能解圍，進亦未晚。」

translations.literal: Heyang is the vital hinge of the realm. The imperial carriage should remain here to stabilize north and south, and meanwhile dispatch a close minister to supervise the fighting. If the siege cannot be lifted, advancing will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Heyang is the vital crossroads of the realm. Your Majesty should remain here to stabilize north and south while sending a close minister to oversee the fighting. If the siege cannot be lifted, advancing later will still be in time."

sentences.zh: 張延朗欲因事令趙延壽得解樞務，因曰：「文紀言是也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang wished to use the occasion to have Zhao Yanshou released from his military affairs commission, and therefore said: "What Wenji says is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang wished to use the occasion to relieve Zhao Yanshou of his military affairs post and said, "Wenji is right."

sentences.zh: 帝訪於餘人，無敢異言者。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted the others; none dared speak differently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the others, and none dared disagree.

sentences.zh: 澤州刺史劉遂凝，鄩之子也，潛自通於石敬瑭，表稱車駕不可逾太行。

translations.literal: Liu Suining, prefect of Zezhou — a son of Zhuang — secretly communicated on his own with Shi Jingtang and memorialized that the imperial carriage must not cross the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Suining, prefect of Zezhou and son of Liu E (Zhuang), had been secretly in contact with Shi Jingtang and memorialized that the emperor must not cross the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 帝議近臣可使北行者，張延朗與翰林學士須昌和凝等詣曰：「趙延壽父德鈞以盧龍兵來赴難，宜遣延壽會之。」

translations.literal: The emperor discussed which close ministers could be sent north. Zhang Yanlang, along with the Hanlin academicians Xu Chang and He Ning and others, presented themselves and said: "Zhao Yanshou's father Dejun is coming with Lulong troops to the rescue — Yanshou should be dispatched to join him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed which close ministers could go north. Zhang Yanlang, together with Hanlin academicians Xu Chang and He Ning and others, came forward and said, "Zhao Yanshou's father Dejun is marching with Lulong troops to the rescue. Yanshou should be sent to join him."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，遣樞密使、忠武節度使、隨駕諸軍都部署、兼侍中趙延壽將兵二萬如潞州。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhao Yanshou, military governor of Zhongwu, overall deployer of all armies accompanying the imperial progress and concurrently palace attendant, was dispatched with twenty thousand troops to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhao Yanshou, military governor of Zhongwu, overall deployer of the armies accompanying the emperor and concurrently palace attendant, was sent with twenty thousand men to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，帝如懷州。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the emperor proceeded to Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the emperor went to Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 以右神武統軍康思立為北面行營馬軍都指揮使，帥扈從騎兵赴團柏谷。

translations.literal: Kang Sili, commander-in-chief of the Right Shenwu army, was made commander of horse troops in the northern campaign headquarters and led the accompanying cavalry to Tuanbaigu.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili, commander-in-chief of the Right Shenwu army, was made northern campaign cavalry commander and led the accompanying horsemen to Tuanbaigu.

sentences.zh: 思立，晉陽胡人也。

translations.literal: Sili was a Hu man of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sili was a Hu tribesman from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝以晉安為憂，問策於群臣，吏部侍郎永清龍敏請立李贊華為契丹主，令天雄、盧龍二鎮分兵送之，自幽州趣西樓，朝廷露檄言之，契丹主必有內顧之憂，然後選募軍中精銳以擊之，此亦解圍之一策也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, anxious about Jin'an, asked the assembled ministers for plans. Long Min, vice minister of Personnel of Yongqing, proposed installing Li Zanhua as Khitan ruler, ordering the Tianxiong and Lulong circuits to divide troops to escort him from Youzhou toward Xilou, and having the court issue an open proclamation to this effect — the Khitan ruler would surely have concern for affairs within, and then selected elite troops from the army could be recruited to strike them. This too was a plan for lifting the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious about Jin'an, the emperor asked his ministers for plans. Long Min, vice minister of Personnel of Yongqing, proposed installing Li Zanhua as Khitan ruler, sending troops from Tianxiong and Lulong to escort him from Youzhou toward Xilou, and issuing an open proclamation from the court. The Khitan ruler would surely look homeward with worry, and then elite troops could be recruited to strike them. This too was a plan for lifting the siege.

sentences.zh: 帝深以為然，而執政恐其無成，議竟不決。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply thought it correct, but those in power feared it would not succeed, and in the end the deliberation was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was strongly persuaded, but the chief ministers feared the plan would fail, and the discussion ended without a decision.

sentences.zh: 帝憂沮形於神色，但日夕酣飲悲歌。

translations.literal: The emperor's worry and dejection showed in his expression and bearing; he only drank heavily and sang sorrowful songs day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Worry and despair showed plainly on the emperor's face; day and night he did nothing but drink heavily and sing dirges.

sentences.zh: 群臣或勸其北行，則曰：「卿勿言，石郎使我心膽墮地！」

translations.literal: When some among the assembled ministers urged him to go north, he would say: "Do not speak of it — Master Shi makes my heart and courage fall to the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: When ministers urged him to march north, he would say, "Say no more — Master Shi has struck my heart dead with terror!"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬戌，詔大括天下將吏及民間馬，又發民為兵，每七戶出征夫一人，自備鎧仗，謂之「義軍」，期以十一月俱集，命陳州刺史郎萬金教以戰陳，用張延朗之謀也。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, an edict ordered a sweeping levy of horses from all generals, officials, and the common people; commoners were also conscripted as soldiers, one conscript laborer from every seven households, each to supply his own armor and weapons — they were called the "Righteous Army" — with orders to assemble entirely in the eleventh month; Chenzhou prefect Lang Wanjin was ordered to teach them battle formations; this followed Zhang Yanlang's plan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, an edict ordered a sweeping levy of horses from all officers and civilians. Civilians were also drafted as soldiers — one man from every seven households, each supplying his own armor and weapons — called the "Righteous Army," to assemble in the eleventh month. Chenzhou prefect Lang Wanjin was ordered to drill them in battle formations. This was Zhang Yanlang's plan.

sentences.zh: 凡得馬二千餘匹，征夫五千人，實無益於用，而民間大擾。

translations.literal: In all they obtained more than two thousand horses and five thousand conscript laborers; in fact there was no benefit to use, yet the common people were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In all they got a little over two thousand horses and five thousand conscripts, which were of little real use, while the countryside was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 初，趙德鈞陰蓄異志，欲因亂取中原，自請救晉安寨；

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhao Dejun secretly harbored divergent designs, wishing to seize the Central Plains amid the turmoil, and on his own requested to rescue Jin'an Stockade;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Dejun had been secretly plotting to seize the Central Plains amid the chaos and volunteered to relieve Jin'an Stockade;

sentences.zh: 唐主命自飛狐踵契丹後，鈔其部落，德鈞請將銀鞍契丹直三千騎，由土門路西入，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor ordered him to follow after the Khitan from Feihu Pass and raid their tribes; Dejun requested to lead three thousand horsemen of the Silver Saddle Khitan Direct unit, entering west by the Tumeng Road, and the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor ordered him to come through Feihu Pass and strike at the Khitan tribes from behind. Dejun asked to lead three thousand Silver Saddle Khitan Direct cavalry west through Tumeng Road, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 趙州刺史、北面行營都指揮使劉在明先將兵戍易州，德鈞過易州，命在明以其眾自隨。

translations.literal: Liu Zaiming, prefect of Zhaozhou and overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters, had earlier led troops to garrison Yizhou; when Dejun passed Yizhou, he ordered Zaiming to bring his forces along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zaiming, prefect of Zhao and overall northern campaign commander, had been garrisoning Yizhou. When Dejun passed through Yizhou, he ordered Zaiming to bring his troops along.

sentences.zh: 在明，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Zaiming was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiming was a native of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 德鈞至鎮州，以董溫琪領招討副使，邀與偕行，又表稱兵少，須合澤潞兵；

translations.literal: When Dejun reached Zhenzhou, he had Dong Wenqi lead as deputy campaign commissioner and invited him to go together; he also memorialized saying his troops were few and must combine with the Ze and Lu forces;
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzhou, Dejun made Dong Wenqi deputy campaign commissioner and invited him along. He also memorialized that his forces were too few and needed to join with the Ze and Lu troops;

sentences.zh: 乃自吳兒谷趣潞州，癸酉，至亂柳。

translations.literal: then he hastened toward Luzhou from Wu'ergu; on guiyou he reached Luanliu.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched toward Luzhou via Wu'ergu and on guiyou reached Luanliu.

sentences.zh: 時范延光受詔將部兵二萬屯遼州，德鈞又請與魏博軍合；

translations.literal: At that time Fan Yanguang had received an edict to lead twenty thousand troops under his command to encamp at Liaozhou; Dejun again requested to join with the Weibo army;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang had been ordered to camp at Liaozhou with twenty thousand men. Dejun again asked to combine with the Weibo army;

sentences.zh: 延光知德鈞合諸軍，志趣難測，表稱魏博兵已入賊境，無容南行數百里與德鈞合，乃止。

translations.literal: Yanguang knew that when Dejun combined the various armies his intent and ambition would be hard to fathom; he memorialized saying the Weibo troops had already entered bandit territory and could not tolerate marching south several hundred li to join Dejun, and so stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang saw that once Dejun united the armies his intentions would be impossible to read. He memorialized that Weibo troops were already in enemy country and could not march south hundreds of li to join Dejun, and the merger was dropped.

sentences.zh: 漢主以宗正卿兼工部侍郎劉濬為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Southern Han ruler made Liu Jun, director of the Imperial Clan and concurrent vice minister of Works, vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han ruler made Liu Jun, director of the Imperial Clan and vice minister of Works, vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 濬，崇望之子也。

translations.literal: Jun was a son of Chongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was the son of Liu Chongwang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子以趙德鈞為諸道行營都統，依前東北面行營招討使。
