translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi Zhao Dejun was made overall commander of the multi-circuit campaign headquarters, continuing as before as northeast campaign pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuzi Zhao Dejun was made overall multi-circuit campaign commander while retaining his post as northeast campaign pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以趙延壽為河東道南面行營招討使，以翰林學士張礪為判官。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou was made southern Hedong campaign pacification commissioner, and Academician Zhang Li was made adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou was made southern Hedong campaign commander, with Academician Zhang Li as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以范延光為河東道東南面行營招討使，以宣武節度使、同平章事李周副之。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Fan Yanguang was made southeast Hedong campaign pacification commissioner, with Li Zhou, military governor of Xuanwu and chief minister, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Fan Yanguang was made southeast Hedong campaign commander, with Li Zhou, military governor of Xuanwu and chief minister, as deputy.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以劉延郎為河東道南面行營招討副使。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Liu Yanlang was made deputy southern Hedong campaign pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Liu Yanlang was made deputy southern Hedong campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽遇趙德鈞於西湯，悉以兵屬德鈞。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou met Zhao Dejun at Xitang and turned over all his troops to Dejun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou met Zhao Dejun at Xitang and placed all his troops under Dejun's command.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣呂琦賜鈞敕告，且犒軍。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor sent Lu Qi to grant Dejun an imperial rescript and moreover reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor sent Lu Qi to deliver an imperial rescript to Dejun and reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 德鈞志在並范延光軍，逗留不進，詔書屢趣之，德鈞乃引兵北屯團柏谷口。

translations.literal: Dejun's aim was to absorb Fan Yanguang's army; he lingered and did not advance. Imperial edicts repeatedly urged him on, and only then did Dejun lead troops north to encamp at Tuanbaigu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun wanted to absorb Fan Yanguang's army and lingered without advancing. Repeated edicts urged him forward, and at last he moved north to camp at Tuanbaigu Pass.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，吳主詔齊主徐知誥置百官，以金陵府為西都。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Wu ruler ordered Qi ruler Xu Zhigao to establish the full bureaucracy of officials and make Jinling Prefecture the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Wu ruler ordered Prince Qi Xu Zhigao to establish a full bureaucracy and designate Jinling Prefecture as the western capital.

sentences.zh: 前坊州刺史劉景巖，延州人也，多財而喜俠，交結豪傑，家有丁夫兵仗，人報其強，勢傾州縣。

translations.literal: Former prefect of Fangzhou Liu Jingyan was a man of Yanzhou; he had much wealth and loved chivalrous deeds, befriending bold heroes; his household had men-at-arms and weapons; people reported his strength, and his power overawed the prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Former Fangzhou prefect Liu Jingyan was from Yanzhou. Rich and fond of chivalry, he befriended local strongmen and kept armed retainers at home. Reports of his power made prefectures and counties fear him.

sentences.zh: 彰武節度使楊漢章無政，失夷、夏心，會括馬及義軍，漢章帥步騎數千人將赴軍期，閱之於野。

translations.literal: Yang Hanzhang, military governor of Zhangwu, was without governance and lost the hearts of both barbarians and Chinese; when the horse levy and volunteer army were mobilized, Hanzhang led several thousand infantry and cavalry about to meet the army muster date and reviewed them in the open field.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hanzhang, military governor of Zhangwu, governed poorly and lost the loyalty of both tribesmen and Han subjects. When the horse levy and volunteer army were called up, Hanzhang led several thousand troops to meet the muster deadline and reviewed them in the field.

sentences.zh: 景巖潛使人撓之曰：「契丹強盛，汝曹有去無歸。」

translations.literal: Jingyan secretly sent men to disturb them, saying: "The Khitan are powerful and flourishing; you all will go but not return.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan secretly sent agents to stir them up, saying, "The Khitan are mighty. You will march out and never come back.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，殺漢章，奉景巖為留後。

translations.literal: The crowd feared this; they killed Hanzhang and made Jingyan acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the troops killed Hanzhang and made Jingyan acting governor.

sentences.zh: 唐主不獲已，丁酉，以景巖為彰武留後。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor, having no alternative, on dingyou made Jingyan acting governor of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor had no choice; on dingyou he recognized Jingyan as acting governor of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 契丹主謂石敬瑭曰：「吾三千里赴難，必有成功。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said to Shi Jingtang: "I have come three thousand li to relieve distress — there will surely be success.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said to Shi Jingtang, "I have marched three thousand li to save you in your distress. Success is certain.

sentences.zh: 觀汝氣貌識量，真中原之主也。

translations.literal: Observing your bearing, appearance, insight, and capacity, you are truly a ruler of the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: From your bearing and your judgment, you are truly fit to rule the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 吾欲立汝為天子。」

translations.literal: I wish to establish you as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to make you emperor.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭辭讓數四，將吏復勸進，乃許之。

translations.literal: Jingtang declined and yielded four or five times; the officers again urged him to accept, and only then did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang declined again and again until his officers pressed him to accept, whereupon he agreed.

sentences.zh: 契丹主作冊書，命敬瑭為大晉皇帝，自解衣冠授之，築壇於柳林。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler drew up an investiture document, appointed Jingtang Grand Emperor of Jin, removed his own robes and cap to invest him, and built an altar at Liulin.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler drafted an investiture charter, named Jingtang emperor of Great Jin, took off his own robes and crowned him, and raised an altar at Liulin.

sentences.zh: 是日，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: That day, he immediately ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 割幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、新、媯、儒、武、雲、應、寰、朔、蔚十六州以與契丹，仍許歲輸帛三十萬匹。

translations.literal: He ceded You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Xin, Gui, Ru, Wu, Yun, Ying, Huan, Shuo, and Wei — sixteen prefectures — to the Khitan, and furthermore pledged an annual tribute of three hundred thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He ceded sixteen prefectures — You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Xin, Gui, Ru, Wu, Yun, Ying, Huan, Shuo, and Wei — to the Khitan and pledged an annual tribute of three hundred thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 己亥，制改長興七年為天福元年，大赦；

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict changed the seventh year of Changxing to the first year of Tianfu, and a general amnesty was proclaimed;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he changed the regnal year from the seventh year of Changxing to the first year of Tianfu and proclaimed a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 敕命法制，皆遵明宗之舊。

translations.literal: edicts, orders, laws, and institutions all followed the former practices of Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: all edicts, institutions, and regulations followed the precedents of Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 以節度判官趙瑩為翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎、知河東軍府事，掌書記桑維翰為翰林學士、禮部侍郎、權知樞密使事，觀察判官薛融為侍御史知雜事，節度推官白水竇貞固為翰林學士，軍城都巡檢使劉知遠為侍衛軍都指揮使，客將景延廣為步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He made Zhao Ying, judge-advocate of the military governorship, Hanlin academician-in-chief and vice minister of Revenue with charge of Hedong army headquarters affairs; Sang Weihan, recorder, Hanlin academician and vice minister of Rites with provisional charge of Privy Council affairs; Xue Rong, judge-advocate of the surveillance commission, attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous matters; Dou Zhengu of Baishui, military governorship legal officer, Hanlin academician; Liu Zhiyuan, metropolitan garrison chief inspector, commander-in-chief of the palace guard army; and Jing Yanguang, guest officer, commander-in-chief of the foot army.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhao Ying, the governor's judge-advocate, Hanlin academician-in-chief and vice minister of Revenue with charge of Hedong headquarters; Sang Weihan, recorder, Hanlin academician and vice minister of Rites with provisional charge of the Privy Council; Xue Rong, surveillance judge, attendant censor with charge of miscellaneous business; Dou Zhengu of Baishui, the governor's legal officer, Hanlin academician; Liu Zhiyuan, metropolitan garrison chief inspector, commander of the palace guards; and Jing Yanguang, guest officer, commander of the foot army.

sentences.zh: 延廣，陝州人也。

translations.literal: Yanguang was a man of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was a native of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 立晉國長公主為皇后。

translations.literal: He established the Princess of Jin State as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He made the Jin State princess empress.

sentences.zh: 契丹主雖軍柳林，其輜重老弱皆在虎北口，每日暝輒結束，以備倉猝遁逃，而趙德鈞欲倚契丹取中國，至團柏逾月，按兵不戰，去晉安才百里，聲問不能相通。

translations.literal: Although the Khitan ruler's army was at Liulin, his baggage train and the old and weak were all at Hubekou; each day at dusk they would pack up to guard against sudden flight in haste. Zhao Dejun wished to rely on the Khitan to seize China; when he reached Tuanbai he stayed over a month, holding his troops and not fighting. He was only a hundred li from Jin'an, yet messages could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Khitan ruler camped at Liulin, his baggage and noncombatants remained at Hubekou, and every evening they packed up lest they have to flee in panic. Zhao Dejun hoped to use the Khitan to take China. At Tuanbai he lingered for over a month without fighting, only a hundred li from Jin'an, yet no word could pass between them.

sentences.zh: 德鈞累表為延壽求成德節度使，曰：「臣今遠征，幽州勢孤，欲使延壽在鎮州，左右便於應接。」

translations.literal: Dejun repeatedly memorialized asking that Yanshou be made military governor of Chengde, saying: "Your servant is now on a distant campaign; Youzhou stands isolated. I wish to have Yanshou at Zhenzhou to facilitate response on either flank.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun repeatedly memorialized to make Yanshou military governor of Chengde, saying, "I am far on campaign and Youzhou stands alone. I want Yanshou at Zhenzhou so he can respond quickly on either side.

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「延壽方擊賊，何暇往鎮州！

translations.literal: The Tang emperor said: "Yanshou is now striking the bandits — what leisure is there to go to Zhenzhou!
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor said, "Yanshou is fighting the enemy now — how can he leave for Zhenzhou!

sentences.zh: 俟賊平，當如所請。」

translations.literal: When the bandits are pacified, your request will be granted as asked.
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy is beaten, I will do as you ask.

sentences.zh: 德鈞求之不已，唐主怒曰：「趙氏父子堅欲得鎮州，何意也？

translations.literal: Dejun pressed the request without cease. The Tang emperor angrily said: "Father and son of the Zhao house obstinately wish to get Zhenzhou — what is their intent?
translations.idiomatic: Dejun would not let up. The Tang emperor burst out, "Why are Zhao father and son so set on getting Zhenzhou?

sentences.zh: 苟能卻胡寇，雖欲代吾位，吾亦甘心，若玩寇邀君，但恐犬兔俱斃耳。」

translations.literal: If they can repel the northern barbarian raiders, even if they wish to replace my throne, I would willingly consent; but if they toy with the enemy and bargain with the ruler, I fear hound and hare will perish together.
translations.idiomatic: If they can drive off the Khitan, they may have my throne and welcome to it. But if they stall the enemy to squeeze concessions from me, I fear we will all die together like the hound and the hare in the fable.

sentences.zh: 德鈞聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: When Dejun heard this, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun took this badly.

sentences.zh: 閏月，趙延壽獻契丹主所賜詔及甲馬弓劍，詐雲德鈞遣使致書於契丹主，為唐結好，說令引兵歸國；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Zhao Yanshou presented the edict, armor, horses, bows, and swords bestowed by the Khitan ruler, falsely saying Dejun had sent envoys with a letter to the Khitan ruler to seek peace with the Tang and persuade him to withdraw his troops and return home;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Zhao Yanshou produced an edict, armor, horses, bows, and swords the Khitan ruler had given him and falsely claimed Dejun had sent envoys asking the Khitan ruler to make peace with the Tang and withdraw;

sentences.zh: 其實別為密書，厚以金帛賂契丹主，云：「若立己為帝，請即以見兵南平洛陽，與契丹為兄弟之國；

translations.literal: In fact he separately prepared a secret letter, bribing the Khitan ruler heavily with gold and silk, saying: "If you establish me as emperor, I beg to use the troops now at hand to pacify Luoyang in the south and make a brotherly state with the Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: In secret he sent a separate letter lavishly bribing the Khitan ruler: "If you make me emperor, I will use the troops I have to pacify Luoyang in the south and we shall be brother states;

sentences.zh: 仍許石氏常鎮河東。」

translations.literal: furthermore allowing the Shi clan to hold Hedong in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: while the Shi clan keeps permanent command of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 契丹主自以深入敵境，晉安未下，德鈞兵尚強，范延光在其東，又恐山北諸州邀其歸路，欲許德鈞之請。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler himself considered that he had penetrated deep into enemy territory; Jin'an had not fallen; Dejun's troops were still strong; Fan Yanguang was to his east; and he also feared the prefectures north of the mountains would intercept his return route — he wished to grant Dejun's request.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler knew he was deep in enemy country, Jin'an still held out, Dejun's army remained strong, Fan Yanguang threatened his east, and the northern prefectures might cut his retreat. He was inclined to accept Dejun's offer.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大懼，亟使桑維翰見契丹主，說之曰：「大國舉義兵以救孤危，一戰而唐兵瓦解，退守一柵，食盡力窮。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and was greatly afraid; he urgently sent Sang Weihan to see the Khitan ruler and persuade him, saying: "The great state raised righteous troops to save one in peril and isolation; in one battle the Tang army collapsed and withdrew to guard a single palisade, food exhausted and strength spent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he was terrified and urgently sent Sang Weihan to the Khitan ruler, who argued: "Your great state came in righteous arms to save us in peril. One battle broke the Tang army and drove them to a single stockade with food gone and strength spent.

sentences.zh: 趙北平父子不忠不信，畏大國之強，且素蓄異志，按兵觀變，非以死徇國之人，何足可畏，而信其誕亡之辭，貪豪末之利，棄垂成之功乎！

translations.literal: Father and son of Zhao the Northern Flatland are disloyal and faithless, fear the great state's strength, and have long harbored divergent designs; they hold their troops and watch for change — they are not men who would die for the state. What is there to fear in them? Why believe their deceitful and desperate words, grasp at a petty profit, and abandon a nearly completed achievement!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun and his son are faithless men who have long plotted rebellion. They hold their troops back and watch which way the wind blows — they would not die for their country. Why fear them, believe their desperate lies, grasp at petty gain, and throw away victory almost in hand!

sentences.zh: 且使晉得天下，將竭中國之財以奉大國，豈此小利之比乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, if Jin obtains the realm, it will exhaust the Central Plains' wealth to serve the great state — how can that be compared with this petty profit!
translations.idiomatic: If Jin wins the realm, it will empty the wealth of China to serve your great state. How does petty bribe money compare with that!

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「爾見捕鼠者乎，不備之，猶或嚙傷其手，況大敵乎！」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "Have you seen a mouse-catcher? Even without taking precautions, he may still be bitten and injured in the hand — how much more so with a great enemy!
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said, "Have you ever seen a mousetrap? Even a mouse may bite your hand if you are not careful — how much more a great foe!

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今大國已扼其喉，安能嚙人乎！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Now the great state already has them by the throat — how can they bite anyone!
translations.idiomatic: Weihan answered, "Your great state already has them by the throat. How can they bite anyone?

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「吾非有渝前約也，但兵家權謀不得不爾。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "I am not violating our former agreement — but in military affairs expedient stratagems cannot but be so.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said, "I do not mean to break our pact, but military expediency leaves no choice.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「皇帝以信義救人之急，四海之人俱屬耳目，奈何一旦二三其命，使大義不終！

translations.literal: He replied: "The emperor with faith and righteousness saves men in urgent peril; all within the four seas are watching and listening — why in one morning and evening change your command twice and thrice, making great righteousness fail to reach its end!
translations.idiomatic: Weihan answered, "Your majesty came in good faith to save us in crisis, and all the world is watching. How can you change your word overnight and leave honor unfinished!

sentences.zh: 臣竊為皇帝不取也。」

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that the emperor ought not take this course.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot believe this is worthy of your majesty.

sentences.zh: 跪於帳前，自旦至暮，涕泣爭之。

translations.literal: He knelt before the tent from dawn till dusk, weeping and disputing this.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt before the tent from dawn to dusk, weeping and pleading.

sentences.zh: 契丹主乃從之，指帳前石謂德鈞使者曰：「我已許石郎，此石爛，可改矣！」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler then yielded to this; pointing to a stone before the tent he said to Dejun's envoys: "I have already promised Master Shi — until this stone rots may this be changed!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler relented. Pointing to a stone before the tent he told Dejun's envoys, "I have promised Master Shi. Not until this stone rots may that be changed!"

sentences.zh: 龍敏謂前鄭州防禦李懿曰：「君，國之近親，今社稷之危，翹足可待，君獨無憂乎？」

translations.literal: Long Min said to former defender of Zhengzhou Li Yi: "You are a close kinsman of the state; now the altars of soil and grain are in danger and can be awaited with one foot lifted — are you alone without worry?
translations.idiomatic: Long Min said to former Zhengzhou defender Li Yi, "You are the emperor's close kin. The realm totters — are you not worried?

sentences.zh: 懿為言趙德鈞必能破敵之狀。

translations.literal: Yi spoke on behalf of the situation that Zhao Dejun would surely be able to break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yi described at length how Zhao Dejun was sure to break the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敏曰：「我燕人也，知德鈞之為人，怯而無謀，但於守城差長耳。

translations.literal: Min said: "I am a man of Yan and know Dejun's character — timid and without strategy, only somewhat skilled at defending cities.
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "I am from Yan and know Dejun. He is timid and unresourceful — only middling at holding cities.

sentences.zh: 況今內蓄奸謀，豈可恃乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, now he secretly harbors treacherous designs — how can he be relied upon!
translations.idiomatic: And now he is plotting treachery within. How can we rely on him!

sentences.zh: 僕有狂策，但恐朝廷不肯為耳。

translations.literal: Your servant has a reckless plan, but I fear the court will not act on it.
translations.idiomatic: I have a bold plan, but I fear the court will not undertake it.

sentences.zh: 今從駕兵尚萬餘人，馬近五千匹，若選精騎一千，使僕與郎萬金將之，自介休山路，夜冒虜騎入晉安寨，但使其半得入，則事濟矣。

translations.literal: Now the troops accompanying the imperial carriage still number more than ten thousand, and horses nearly five thousand; if one selects a thousand elite horsemen and has your servant and Lang Wanjin lead them by the Jiexiu mountain road, by night braving the barbarian riders to enter Jin'an Stockade — if even half can get in, the affair will succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still has more than ten thousand troops and nearly five thousand horses. Choose a thousand elite cavalry and let me and Lang Wanjin lead them through the Jiexiu mountain road by night past the enemy horsemen into Jin'an Stockade. If even half get through, it will succeed.

sentences.zh: 張敬達等陷於重圍，不知朝廷聲問，若知大軍近在團柏，雖有鐵障可衝陷，況虜騎乎！」

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda and the others are trapped in heavy encirclement and do not know the court's news; if they knew the great army is close at Tuanbai, though there were an iron barrier they could break through — how much more so barbarian horsemen!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda and the rest are trapped in siege and know nothing of the court. If they knew a great army was near at Tuanbai, they could smash through an iron wall — how much more Khitan cavalry!

sentences.zh: 懿以白唐主，唐主曰：「龍敏之志極壯，用之晚矣。」

translations.literal: Yi reported this to the Tang emperor, and the Tang emperor said: "Long Min's ambition is extremely bold — employing it is already too late."
translations.idiomatic: Yi told the Tang emperor, who said, "Long Min's spirit is magnificent — but it is too late to use it."

sentences.zh: 丹州義軍作亂，逐刺史康承詢，承詢奔鄜州。

translations.literal: The volunteer army of Danzhou mutinied, drove out prefect Kang Chengzhong, and Chengzhong fled to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Danzhou volunteer army mutinied, expelled prefect Kang Chengzhong, and Chengzhong fled to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉安寨被圍數月，高行周、符彥卿數引騎兵出戰，眾寡不敵，皆無功。

translations.literal: Jin'an Stockade was besieged for several months; Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing repeatedly led cavalry out to battle; outnumbered, they achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin'an Stockade had been under siege for months. Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing led cavalry out again and again, but they were too few and gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 芻糧俱竭，削柹淘糞以飼馬，馬相啖，尾鬣皆禿，死則將士分食之，援兵竟不至。

translations.literal: Fodder and grain were both exhausted; they whittled bark and rinsed dung to feed the horses; the horses devoured one another, tails and manes all bare; when they died the officers and soldiers divided the flesh to eat, and relief troops in the end never arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder and grain ran out. They scraped bark and washed dung to feed the horses; the horses ate one another until their tails and manes fell out. When a horse died the soldiers ate its flesh. Relief never came.

sentences.zh: 張敬達性剛，時謂之「張生鐵。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda's nature was hard; at the time they called him "Zhang Raw Iron."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda was unyielding by nature; men called him "Iron Zhang."

sentences.zh: 楊光遠、安審琦，勸敬達降於契丹，敬達曰：「吾受明宗及今上厚恩，為元帥而敗軍，其罪已大，況降敵乎！

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan and An Shenqi urged Jingda to surrender to the Khitan. Jingda said: "I have received great grace from Mingzong and the present sovereign; as commander-in-chief to fail the army — that crime is already great — how much more to surrender to the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan and An Shenqi urged Jingda to surrender to the Khitan. Jingda said, "Mingzong and the present emperor have shown me great favor. As commander I have already failed my army — that is crime enough. How could I surrender to the enemy!

sentences.zh: 今援兵旦暮至，且當俟之。

translations.literal: Now relief troops will arrive at dawn or dusk; for the time being we should await them.
translations.idiomatic: Relief is almost here. We must wait.

sentences.zh: 必若力盡勢窮，則諸軍斬我首，攜之出降，自求多福，未為晚也。」

translations.literal: If strength is exhausted and the situation desperate, then let the various armies cut off my head, carry it out to surrender, and seek their own good fortune — that would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we reach the end of our strength, cut off my head and carry it out to surrender and save yourselves. That will still be in time.

sentences.zh: 光遠目審琦欲殺敬達，審琦未忍。

translations.literal: Guangyuan signaled Shenqi with his eyes, wishing to kill Jingda, but Shenqi could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan signaled Shenqi to kill Jingda, but Shenqi could not bring himself to do it.

sentences.zh: 高行周知光遠欲圖敬達，常引壯騎尾而衛之，敬達不知其故，謂人曰：「行周每踵余後，何意也？」

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou knew Guangyuan wished to plot against Jingda and often led strong horsemen to follow at his heels and guard him. Jingda did not know the reason and said to others: "Xingzhou always treads on my heels — what is his meaning?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou knew Guangyuan meant to kill Jingda and often rode behind him with strong cavalry as guard. Jingda did not know why and said, "Why does Xingzhou always follow at my heels?

sentences.zh: 行周乃不敢隨之。

translations.literal: Xingzhou then dared not follow after him.
translations.idiomatic: After that Xingzhou no longer dared follow him.

sentences.zh: 諸將每旦集於招討使營，甲子，高行周、符彥卿未至，光遠乘其無備，斬敬達首，帥諸將上表降於契丹。

translations.literal: Each morning the generals gathered at the campaign commissioner's camp. On jiazi, Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing had not yet arrived; Guangyuan seized their unpreparedness, beheaded Jingda, and leading the generals submitted a memorial surrendering to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The generals met each morning at the campaign commissioner's camp. On jiazi, before Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing arrived, Guangyuan caught them off guard, beheaded Jingda, and led the generals in surrendering to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹主素聞諸將名，皆慰勞，賜以裘帽，因戲之曰：「汝輩亦大惡漢，不用鹽酪啖戰馬萬匹！」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler had long heard the generals' names; he consoled and rewarded them all and gave fur coats and caps, then jokingly said to them: "You are also great wicked Han — feeding ten thousand war horses without salt or curds!
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler, who had long known the generals by name, received them with praise and gifts of fur coats and caps, then joked, "You wretched Han — ten thousand war horses fed without a grain of salt or curds!

sentences.zh: 光遠等大慚。

translations.literal: Guangyuan and the others were greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan and the rest were deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 契丹主嘉張敬達之忠，命收葬而祭之，謂其下及晉諸將曰：「汝曹為人臣，當效敬達也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler praised Zhang Jingda's loyalty, ordered his body collected and buried and sacrifices performed for him, and said to his subordinates and the Jin generals: "You all as subject-ministers ought to emulate Jingda."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler honored Zhang Jingda's loyalty, had him buried with rites, and told his men and the Jin generals, "As subjects you should be like Jingda."

sentences.zh: 時晉安寨馬猶近五千，鎧仗五萬，契丹悉取以歸其國，悉以唐之將卒授帝，語之曰：「勉事而主。」

translations.literal: At that time Jin'an Stockade still had nearly five thousand horses and fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons; the Khitan took them all back to his state and handed over all the Tang officers and soldiers to the emperor, telling them: "Serve your lord with diligence."
translations.idiomatic: Jin'an still had nearly five thousand horses and fifty thousand sets of arms. The Khitan took them all home and handed the Tang officers and soldiers to the emperor, saying, "Serve your lord faithfully."

sentences.zh: 馬軍都指揮使康思立憤惋而死。

translations.literal: Kang Sili, commander-in-chief of the horse army, died of indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili, commander of the horse army, died of rage and grief.

sentences.zh: 帝以晉安已降，遣使諭諸州。

translations.literal: The emperor, since Jin'an had surrendered, sent envoys to instruct the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin'an fell, the emperor sent envoys to notify the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 代州刺史張朗斬其使；

translations.literal: Zhang Lang, prefect of Daizhou, beheaded the envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang, prefect of Dai, executed the envoy;

sentences.zh: 呂琦奉唐主詔勞北軍，至忻州，遇晉使，亦斬之，謂刺史丁審琦曰：「虜過城下而不顧，其心可見，還日必無全理，不若早帥兵民自五台奔鎮州。」

translations.literal: Lu Qi, bearing the Tang emperor's edict to reward the northern army, reached Xinzhou, encountered the Jin envoy, and also beheaded him; he said to prefect Ding Shenqi: "When the barbarians pass below the city walls without a glance, their intent is clear — on the day they return there will surely be no survival; better early to lead troops and people from Wutai to flee to Zhenzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi had been sent by the Tang emperor to reward the northern army. At Xinzhou he met a Jin envoy and killed him too. He told prefect Ding Shenqi, "The Khitan marched past this city without a look — you can see their mind. When they return this place cannot stand. Better lead troops and people from Wutai to flee to Zhenzhou now.

sentences.zh: 將行，審琦悔之，閉牙城不從。

translations.literal: About to depart, Shenqi repented of this, closed the administrative city and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to leave, Shenqi changed his mind, shut the yamen gate, and refused.

sentences.zh: 州兵欲攻之，琦曰：「家國如此，何為復相屠滅！」

translations.literal: The prefecture troops wished to attack him; Qi said: "State and family are already thus — why commit mutual slaughter again!
translations.idiomatic: The garrison wanted to attack him. Qi said, "The realm is ruined — why slaughter one another?

sentences.zh: 乃帥州兵趣鎮州，審琦遂降契丹。

translations.literal: He then led the prefecture troops toward Zhenzhou, and Shenqi thereupon surrendered to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He led the garrison to Zhenzhou instead, and Shenqi surrendered to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹主謂帝曰：「桑維翰盡忠於汝，宜以為相。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said to the emperor: "Sang Weihan is wholly loyal to you — he ought to be made chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler told the emperor, "Sang Weihan has been utterly loyal to you. Make him chief minister."

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以趙瑩為門下侍郎，桑維翰為中書侍郎，並同平章事；

translations.literal: On bingyin, Zhao Ying was made vice director of the Chancellery and Sang Weihan vice director of the Secretariat, both concurrent chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Zhao Ying was made vice director of the Chancellery and Sang Weihan vice director of the Secretariat, both chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 維翰仍權知樞密使事。

translations.literal: Weihan still provisionally managed Privy Council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan continued in provisional charge of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 以楊光遠為侍衛馬步軍都指揮使，以劉知遠為保義節度使、侍衛馬步軍都虞侯。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan was made commander-in-chief of palace guard horse and foot; Liu Zhiyuan was made military governor of Baoyi and deputy commander-in-chief of palace guard horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan was made commander of the palace horse and foot armies; Liu Zhiyuan was made military governor of Baoyi and deputy commander of the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 帝與契丹主將引兵而南，欲留一子守河東，咨於契丹主，契丹主令帝盡出諸子，自擇之。

translations.literal: The emperor and the Khitan ruler were about to lead troops south; wishing to leave one son to guard Hedong, he consulted the Khitan ruler, who ordered the emperor to bring out all his sons and choose for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the Khitan ruler prepared to march south. Wanting to leave a son to guard Hedong, he asked the Khitan ruler, who told him to parade all his sons and choose.

sentences.zh: 帝兄子重貴，父敬儒早卒，帝養以為子，貌類帝而短小，契丹主指之曰：「此大目者可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor's brother's son Chonggui — his father Jingru had died early, and the emperor raised him as a son — resembled the emperor in appearance though he was short in stature; the Khitan ruler pointed to him and said: "This one with the large eyes will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's nephew Chonggui — his father Jingru had died young and the emperor had raised him as a son — looked like the emperor though he was small. The Khitan ruler pointed at him and said, "This big-eyed one will do."

sentences.zh: 乃以重貴為北京留守、太原尹、河東節度使。

translations.literal: He then appointed Chonggui northern capital regent, prefect of Taiyuan, and military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Chonggui regent of the northern capital, prefect of Taiyuan, and military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 契丹以其將高謨翰為前鋒，與降卒偕進。

translations.literal: The Khitan made their general Gao Mo'han vanguard and advanced together with surrendered troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan put their general Gao Mo'han in the van and marched on together with the surrendered troops.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至團柏，與唐兵戰，趙德鈞、趙延壽先循，符彥饒、張彥琦、劉延朗、劉在明繼之，士卒大潰，相騰踐死者萬計。

translations.literal: On dingmao they reached Tuanbai and fought Tang troops. Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou fled first; Fu Yanrao, Zhang Yanqi, Liu Yanlang, and Liu Zaiming followed suit. The soldiers broke completely; those trampled to death in the crush numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao they reached Tuanbai and clashed with Tang forces. Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou fled first, and Fu Yanrao, Zhang Yanqi, Liu Yanlang, and Liu Zaiming followed. The army collapsed utterly; tens of thousands were trampled to death in the stampede.

sentences.zh: 己巳，延朗、在明至懷州，唐主始知帝即位，楊光遠降。

translations.literal: On jisi Yanlang and Zaiming reached Huai Prefecture. The Tang emperor only then learned that the emperor had ascended the throne; Yang Guangyuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Yanlang and Zaiming reached Huai Prefecture. Only then did the Tang emperor learn that the new emperor had taken the throne, and Yang Guangyuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 眾議以「天雄軍府尚完，契丹秘憚山東，未敢南下，車駕宜幸魏州。」

translations.literal: The assembly argued that "the Tianxiong headquarters is still intact, the Khitan secretly dread advancing into Shandong and dare not march south — the imperial carriage ought to proceed to Weizhou."
translations.idiomatic: The court debated that "the Tianxiong headquarters is still intact, the Khitan secretly fear advancing into Shandong and dare not push south — the imperial carriage should go to Weizhou."

sentences.zh: 唐主以李崧素與范延光善，召崧謀之。

translations.literal: As Li Song was on good terms with Fan Yanguang, the Tang emperor summoned Song to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Song was on good terms with Fan Yanguang, the Tang emperor summoned Song to discuss the plan.

sentences.zh: 薛文遇不知而繼至，唐主怒，變色；

translations.literal: Xue Wenyü arrived next without knowing, and the Tang emperor grew angry, his face changing color;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wenyü arrived next, unaware of what was afoot, and the Tang emperor flew into a rage, his face darkening;

sentences.zh: 崧躡文遇足，文遇乃去。

translations.literal: Song trod on Wenyü's foot, and Wenyü then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Song stepped on Wenyü's foot, and Wenyü withdrew.

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「我見此物肉顫，適幾欲抽佩刀刺之。」

translations.literal: The Tang emperor said: "When I see this creature my flesh trembles — I was just about to draw my girdle-dagger and stab him."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor said, "When I see that creature my flesh crawls — I was just about to draw my dagger and run him through."

sentences.zh: 崧曰：「文遇小人，淺謀國，刺之益丑。」

translations.literal: Song said: "Wenyü is a petty man who plotted shallowly against the state; stabbing him would only make things uglier."
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "Wenyü is a petty man who schemed shallowly against the state. Stabbing him would only make matters uglier."

sentences.zh: 崧因勸唐主南還，唐主從之。

translations.literal: Song thereupon urged the Tang emperor to return south, and the Tang emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Song then urged the Tang emperor to turn south, and the Tang emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 洛陽聞北軍敗，眾心大震，居人四出，逃竄山谷。

translations.literal: When Luoyang heard that the northern army had been defeated, hearts were greatly shaken; residents fled in all directions, scattering into mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang heard that the northern army had been defeated, panic seized the city. Residents fled in every direction, scattering into the hills and valleys.

sentences.zh: 門者請禁之，河南尹雍王重美曰：「國家多難，未能為百姓主，又禁其求生，徒增惡名耳；

translations.literal: The gatekeepers asked to forbid it. Fan Wang Chongmei, prefect of Henan, said: "The state is in great trouble and cannot yet act as master for the people; to forbid them seeking life would only add to our ill repute;
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers asked to stop them. Fan Wang Chongmei, prefect of Henan, said, "The state is in crisis and cannot yet protect its people. To forbid them from saving themselves would only deepen our ill repute;

sentences.zh: 不若聽其自便，事寧自還。」

translations.literal: better to let them go as they please — when things calm they will return of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: better to let them go where they will. When things settle, they will return on their own."

sentences.zh: 乃出令任從所適，眾心差安。

translations.literal: An order was issued allowing people to go wherever they wished, and hearts were somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued allowing people to go wherever they chose, and hearts were somewhat calmed.

sentences.zh: 壬申，唐主還至河陽，命諸將分守南、北城。

translations.literal: On renshen the Tang emperor returned to Heyang and ordered the generals to divide and hold the southern and northern cities.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Tang emperor returned to Heyang and ordered his generals to divide and hold the southern and northern cities.

sentences.zh: 張延朗請幸滑州，庶與魏博聲勢相接，唐主不能決。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang asked that the court proceed to Huazhou, so as to link forces with Weibo; the Tang emperor could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang urged the court to move to Huazhou so its strength could join Weibo's, but the Tang emperor could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 趙德鈞、趙延壽南奔潞州，唐敗兵稍稍從之，其將時賽帥盧龍輕騎東還漁陽。

translations.literal: Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou fled south to Luzhou; Tang defeated troops gradually followed them. Their general Shi Sai led Lulong light cavalry east back to Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun and Zhao Yanshou fled south to Luzhou, and defeated Tang troops gradually joined them. Their general Shi Sai led Lulong light cavalry east back to Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 帝先遣昭義節度使高行周還具食，至城下，見德鈞父子在城上，行周曰：「僕與大王鄉曲，敢不忠告！

translations.literal: The emperor first sent Zhaoyi military governor Gao Xingzhou back to prepare provisions. When he reached the walls and saw Dejun and his son on the ramparts, Xingzhou said: "I am from your home district, my lord — how could I fail to speak frankly!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first sent Zhaoyi military governor Gao Xingzhou back to prepare provisions. When he reached the walls and saw Dejun and his son on the ramparts, Xingzhou said, "We are from the same home district, my lord — how could I fail to speak plainly!

sentences.zh: 城中無斗粟可寧，不若速迎車駕。」

translations.literal: There is not a bushel of grain in the city to keep you at ease — better to hurry and welcome the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: There is not a bushel of grain in the city to sustain you. Better to hurry and welcome the imperial carriage."

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝與契丹主至潞州，德鈞父子迎謁於高河，契丹主慰諭之，父子拜帝於馬首，進曰：「別後安否？」

translations.literal: On jiaxu the emperor and the Khitan ruler reached Luzhou. Dejun and his son welcomed them at Gaohe. The Khitan ruler comforted and instructed them; father and son bowed to the emperor at his horse's head and stepped forward saying: "After our parting, are you well?"
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the emperor and the Khitan ruler reached Luzhou. Dejun and his son welcomed them at Gaohe. The Khitan ruler comforted them, and father and son bowed to the emperor at his horse's head and asked, "Since we parted, have you been well?"

sentences.zh: 帝不顧，亦不與之言。

translations.literal: The emperor paid no heed and did not speak with them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them and would not speak a word.

sentences.zh: 契丹主謂德鈞曰：「汝在幽州所置銀鞍契丹直何在？」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said to Dejun: "Where are the Silver-Saddle Khitan guards you established at Youzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler said to Dejun, "Where are the Silver-Saddle Khitan guards you posted at Youzhou?"

sentences.zh: 德鈞指示之，契丹主命盡殺之於西郊，凡三千人。

translations.literal: Dejun pointed them out; the Khitan ruler ordered all killed in the western suburbs — three thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun pointed them out, and the Khitan ruler ordered all three thousand killed in the western suburbs.

sentences.zh: 遂瑣德鈞、延壽，送歸其國。

translations.literal: He then put Dejun and Yanshou in chains and sent them back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: He then put Dejun and Yanshou in chains and sent them back to Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 德鈞見述律太后，悉以所賚寶貨並籍其田宅獻之，太后問曰：「汝近者何為往太原？」

translations.literal: Dejun saw Empress Dowager Shulü and presented all the treasure he had been rewarded plus a register of his fields and houses. The empress dowager asked: "Why did you recently go to Taiyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Dejun appeared before Empress Dowager Shulü and presented all the treasure he had received, along with a register of his fields and houses. The empress dowager asked, "Why did you go to Taiyuan recently?"

sentences.zh: 德鈞曰：「奉唐主之命。」

translations.literal: Dejun said: "I obeyed the Tang emperor's command."
translations.idiomatic: Dejun said, "I was acting on the Tang emperor's orders."

sentences.zh: 太后指天曰：「汝從吾兒求為天子，何亡語邪！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager pointed to heaven and said: "You asked my son to make you emperor — why this dead language!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager pointed to heaven and said, "You asked my son to make you emperor — why this empty talk!"

sentences.zh: 又自指其心曰：「此不可欺也。」

translations.literal: She also pointed to her own heart and said: "This cannot be deceived."
translations.idiomatic: Then she pointed to her own heart and said, "This cannot be deceived."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「吾兒將行，吾戒之云：趙大王若引兵北向渝關，亟須引歸，太原可救也。

translations.literal: She also said: "When my son was about to march, I warned him: 'If Prince Zhao leads troops north toward Yuguan, you must quickly withdraw — Taiyuan can still be saved.
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "When my son was about to march, I warned him: 'If Prince Zhao leads troops north toward Yuguan, you must withdraw at once — Taiyuan can still be saved.

sentences.zh: 汝欲為天子，何不先擊退吾兒，徐圖亦未晚。

translations.literal: If you wished to be emperor, why not first strike and drive off my son? To plot at leisure afterward would not have been too late.
translations.idiomatic: If you wanted to be emperor, why not first drive my son off and only then plot at leisure? That would not have been too late.

sentences.zh: 汝為人臣，既負其主，不能擊敵，又欲乘亂邀利，所為如此，何面目復求生乎？」

translations.literal: You were a subject — you betrayed your lord, could not strike the enemy, yet wished to seize advantage amid chaos. Having acted thus, with what face could you still seek to live?"
translations.idiomatic: You were a subject. You betrayed your lord, failed to strike the enemy, yet hoped to profit from the chaos. Having acted like this, with what face could you still seek to live?"

sentences.zh: 德鈞俯首不能對。

translations.literal: Dejun bowed his head and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun bowed his head and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 又問：「器玩在此，田宅何在？」

translations.literal: She asked again: "The vessels and curios are here — where are the fields and houses?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked again, "The vessels and curios are here — where are the fields and houses?"

sentences.zh: 德鈞曰：「在幽州。」

translations.literal: Dejun said: "At Youzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Dejun said, "At Youzhou."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「幽州今屬誰？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Youzhou now belongs to whom?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Youzhou belongs to whom now?"

sentences.zh: 德鈞曰：「屬太后。」

translations.literal: Dejun said: "To Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Dejun said, "To Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「然則又何獻焉？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Then what is there to present?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Then what is there to present?"

sentences.zh: 德鈞益慚。

translations.literal: Dejun grew all the more ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun grew all the more ashamed.

sentences.zh: 自是鬱鬱不多食，逾年而卒。

translations.literal: From then on he was despondent and ate little; after more than a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he sank into gloom and ate little. After more than a year he died.

sentences.zh: 張礪與延壽俱入契丹，契丹主復以為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Zhang Li and Yanshou both entered Khitan territory; the Khitan ruler again made Li a Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li and Yanshou both entered Khitan territory, and the Khitan ruler again made Li a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 帝將發上黨，契丹主舉酒屬帝曰：「余遠來徇義，今大事已成，我若南向，河南之人必大驚核；

translations.literal: As the emperor was about to set out from Shangdang, the Khitan ruler raised his cup and addressed the emperor: "I came far to serve righteousness; now the great affair is accomplished. If I march south, the people of Henan will be greatly alarmed;
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to leave Shangdang, the Khitan ruler raised his cup and addressed him: "I came from afar to serve righteousness, and now the great affair is done. If I march south, the people of Henan will be terrified;

sentences.zh: 汝宜自引漢兵南下，人必不甚懼。

translations.literal: you ought to lead Han troops south yourself — the people will not be very afraid.
translations.idiomatic: you should lead Han troops south yourself. The people will not be so afraid.

sentences.zh: 我令太相溫將五千騎衛送汝至河梁，欲與之渡河者多少隨意，余且留此，俟汝音聞，有急則下山救汝。

translations.literal: I will have Grand Chancellor Wen lead five thousand horsemen to escort you to Heliang. As many as wish to cross the river with you may do as they please. I shall remain here awaiting word from you; if there is urgency I will come down from the mountains to save you.
translations.idiomatic: I will have Grand Chancellor Wen lead five thousand horsemen to escort you to Heliang. As many as wish to cross the river with you may do so. I shall stay here and wait for word from you, and if you are in danger I will come down from the mountains to save you.

sentences.zh: 若洛陽既定，吾即北返矣。」

translations.literal: If Luoyang is settled, I shall at once return north."
translations.idiomatic: Once Luoyang is secure, I shall return north at once."

sentences.zh: 與帝執手相泣，久之不能別，解白貂裘以衣帝，贈良馬二十匹，戰馬千二百匹，曰：「世世子孫勿相忘！」

translations.literal: He grasped the emperor's hand and they wept together; long they could not part. He took off his white sable coat to clothe the emperor, gave twenty fine horses and twelve hundred war horses, and said: "Generation after generation — let our descendants not forget one another!"
translations.idiomatic: He took the emperor's hand and they wept together, unable to part for a long while. He removed his white sable coat and put it on the emperor, gave him twenty fine horses and twelve hundred war horses, and said, "Generation after generation — let our descendants never forget one another!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「劉知遠、趙瑩、桑維翰皆創業功臣，無大故，勿棄也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Liu Zhiyuan, Zhao Ying, and Sang Weihan are all founders of the enterprise — unless there is grave cause, do not discard them."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Liu Zhiyuan, Zhao Ying, and Sang Weihan are all founders of your enterprise. Unless there is grave cause, do not cast them aside."

sentences.zh: 初，張敬達既出師，唐主遣左金吾大將軍歷山高漢筠守晉州。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Zhang Jingda had marched out, the Tang emperor sent Left Golden Guard senior general Gao Hanyun of Lishan to hold Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Zhang Jingda had marched out, the Tang emperor sent Left Golden Guard senior general Gao Hanyun of Lishan to hold Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敬達死，建雄節度使田承肇帥眾攻漢筠於府署，漢筠開門延承肇入，從容謂曰：「僕與公俱受朝寄，何相迫如此？」

translations.literal: After Jingda died, Jianxiong military governor Tian Chengzhao led troops to attack Hanyun at the headquarters. Hanyun opened the gate and admitted Chengzhao, then said calmly: "You and I alike bear the court's commission — why press me so?"
translations.idiomatic: After Jingda died, Jianxiong military governor Tian Chengzhao led troops to attack Hanyun at the headquarters. Hanyun opened the gate and admitted Chengzhao, then said calmly, "You and I alike bear the court's commission — why press me so hard?"

sentences.zh: 承肇曰：「欲奉公為節度使。」

translations.literal: Chengzhao said: "I wish to install you as military governor."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao said, "I mean to install you as military governor."

sentences.zh: 漢筠曰：「僕老矣，義不為亂首，死生惟公所處。」

translations.literal: Hanyun said: "I am old; by principle I will not be the head of rebellion — life and death are for you to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Hanyun said, "I am old. By principle I will not lead a rebellion — life and death are yours to decide."

sentences.zh: 承肇目左右欲殺之，軍士投刃於地曰：「高金吾累朝宿德，奈何害之！」

translations.literal: Chengzhao signaled his attendants to kill him, but the soldiers cast their blades to the ground and said: "Commander Gao of the Golden Guard is honored through many reigns — how could we harm him!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao signaled his attendants to kill him, but the soldiers cast their blades to the ground and cried, "Commander Gao of the Golden Guard is honored through many reigns — how could we harm him!"

sentences.zh: 承肇乃謝曰：「與公戲耳。」

translations.literal: Chengzhao then apologized: "I was only jesting with you."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhao then apologized, "I was only jesting with you."

sentences.zh: 聽漢筠歸洛陽。

translations.literal: He allowed Hanyun to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed Hanyun to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝遇諸塗，曰：「朕憂卿為亂兵所傷，今見卿甚喜。」

translations.literal: The emperor encountered him on the road and said: "I feared you might be harmed by mutinous troops — to see you now gives me great joy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor met him on the road and said, "I feared you might be harmed by mutinous troops. To see you now fills me with joy."

sentences.zh: 符彥饒、張彥琪至河陽，密言於唐主曰：「今胡兵大下，河水復淺，人心已離，此不可守。」

translations.literal: Fu Yanrao and Zhang Yanqi reached Heyang and said secretly to the Tang emperor: "Now barbarian troops are descending in force, the river water is again shallow, and hearts have already turned away — this place cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanrao and Zhang Yanqi reached Heyang and said secretly to the Tang emperor, "Barbarian troops are descending in force, the river is shallow again, and hearts have already turned away. This place cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 丁丑，唐主命河陽節度使萇從簡與趙州刺史劉在明守河陽南城，遂斷浮梁，歸洛陽。

translations.literal: On dingchou the Tang emperor ordered Heyang military governor Chang Congjian and Zhao Prefecture prefect Liu Zaiming to hold the southern city of Heyang, then cut the pontoon bridge and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Tang emperor ordered Heyang military governor Chang Congjian and Zhao Prefecture prefect Liu Zaiming to hold the southern city of Heyang, then cut the pontoon bridge and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遣宦者秦繼旻、皇城使李彥紳殺昭信節度使李贊華於其第。

translations.literal: He sent eunuchs Qin Jimin and Li Yanshen, commissioner of the Imperial City, to kill Zhaoxin military governor Li Zanhua at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He sent eunuchs Qin Jimin and Li Yanshen, commissioner of the Imperial City, to kill Zhaoxin military governor Li Zanhua at his residence.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝至河陽，萇從簡迎降，舟楫已具。

translations.literal: On jimao the emperor reached Heyang; Chang Congjian came out to surrender, and boats were already prepared.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the emperor reached Heyang. Chang Congjian came out to surrender, and boats were already prepared.

sentences.zh: 彰聖軍執劉在明以降，帝釋之，使復其所。

translations.literal: The Zhangsheng army seized Liu Zaiming to surrender; the emperor released him and restored him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangsheng army seized Liu Zaiming and brought him over. The emperor released him and restored him to his post.

sentences.zh: 唐主命馬軍都指揮使宋審虔、步軍都指揮使符彥饒、河陽節度使張彥琪、宣徽南院使劉延朗將千餘騎至白馬阪行戰地，有五十餘騎渡河奔於北軍。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor ordered horse army commander Song Shenqian, foot army commander Fu Yanrao, Heyang military governor Zhang Yanqi, and southern commissioner of the Palace Directorate Liu Yanlang to lead a thousand-odd horsemen to Baima Slope to reconnoiter the battlefield; more than fifty horsemen crossed the river and fled to the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor ordered horse army commander Song Shenqian, foot army commander Fu Yanrao, Heyang military governor Zhang Yanqi, and southern commissioner of the Palace Directorate Liu Yanlang to lead more than a thousand horsemen to Baima Slope to reconnoiter the battlefield. More than fifty horsemen crossed the river and fled to the northern army.

sentences.zh: 諸將謂審虔曰：「何地不可戰，誰肯立於此？」

translations.literal: The generals said to Shenqian: "Where could one not fight — who would stand here?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals said to Shenqian, "Where could one not fight — who would stand here?"

sentences.zh: 乃還。

translations.literal: They then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned back.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，唐主又與四將議復向河陽，而將校皆已飛狀迎帝。

translations.literal: On gengchen the Tang emperor again discussed with the four generals returning toward Heyang, but officers and soldiers had all already sent urgent messages welcoming the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Tang emperor again discussed with the four generals returning toward Heyang, but officers and soldiers had already sent urgent messages welcoming the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝慮唐主西奔，遣契丹千騎扼澠池。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing the Tang emperor would flee west, sent a thousand Khitan horsemen to hold Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Tang emperor would flee west, the emperor sent a thousand Khitan horsemen to hold Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，唐主與曹太后、劉皇后、雍王重美及宋審虔等攜傳國寶登玄武樓自焚，皇后積薪欲燒宮室，重美諫曰：「新天子至，必不露居，他日重勞民力；

translations.literal: On xinsi the Tang emperor, with Empress Dowager Cao, Empress Liu, Prince of Yong Chongmei, and Song Shenqian and others, took the imperial seals and ascended the Xuanwu Tower to immolate themselves. The empress piled firewood intending to burn the palace halls. Chongmei remonstrated: "When the new Son of Heaven arrives, he will surely not live exposed to the elements — to burn the halls would later again exhaust the people's strength;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Tang emperor, with Empress Dowager Cao, Empress Liu, Prince of Yong Chongmei, and Song Shenqian and others, took the imperial seals and ascended the Xuanwu Tower to burn themselves. The empress piled firewood intending to burn the palace halls. Chongmei remonstrated, "When the new Son of Heaven arrives, he will surely not live exposed to the weather. To burn the halls would later exhaust the people's strength again;

sentences.zh: 死而遺怨，將安用之！」

translations.literal: to die and leave behind resentment — what use is that!"
translations.idiomatic: to die and leave behind resentment — what use is that!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They then stopped.

sentences.zh: 王淑妃謂太后曰：「事急矣，宜且避匿，以俟姑夫。」

translations.literal: Consort Wang Shufei said to the empress dowager: "The matter is urgent — you ought for now to hide and await your brother-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang Shufei said to the empress dowager, "The matter is urgent. You ought to hide for now and await your brother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「吾子孫婦女一朝至此，何忍獨生！

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "My sons, grandchildren, and daughters-in-law have come to this in a single morning — how could I bear to live alone!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "My sons, grandchildren, and daughters-in-law have come to this in a single morning — how could I bear to live alone!

sentences.zh: 妹自勉之。」

translations.literal: Sister, encourage yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Sister, take heart."

sentences.zh: 淑妃乃與許王從益匿於球場，獲免。

translations.literal: Shufei then hid with Prince Xu Congyi in the ball ground and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shufei then hid with Prince Xu Congyi in the ball ground and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 是日晚，帝入洛陽，止於舊第。

translations.literal: That same evening the emperor entered Luoyang and lodged at his old residence.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening the emperor entered Luoyang and lodged at his old residence.

sentences.zh: 唐兵皆解甲待罪，帝慰而釋之。

translations.literal: Tang troops all doffed armor to await punishment; the emperor comforted and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops all doffed their armor to await punishment. The emperor comforted them and released them.

sentences.zh: 帝命劉知遠部署京城，知遠分漢軍使還營，館契丹於天宮寺，城中肅然，無敢犯令。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Liu Zhiyuan to deploy the capital. Zhiyuan sent Han troops back to their camps and quartered the Khitan at Tiangong Temple. The city was orderly; none dared violate the orders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Liu Zhiyuan to secure the capital. Zhiyuan sent Han troops back to their camps and quartered the Khitan at Tiangong Temple. The city was orderly, and none dared break the rules.

sentences.zh: 士民避亂竄匿者，數日皆還復業。

translations.literal: Civil officials and commoners who had fled and hidden from the turmoil all returned within days to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners who had fled and hidden from the turmoil all returned within days to resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在河東，為唐朝所忌，中書侍郎、同平章事、判三司張延朗不欲河東多蓄積，凡財賦應留使之外盡收取之，帝以是恨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while the emperor was in Hedong he was viewed with suspicion by the Tang court. Secretariat vice director, chief minister, and acting Three Commissions director Zhang Yanlang did not wish Hedong to accumulate much wealth; beyond what the military governor was permitted to retain, he took all revenue and supplies. The emperor therefore resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was in Hedong the Tang court viewed him with suspicion. Secretariat vice director, chief minister, and acting Three Commissions director Zhang Yanlang did not want Hedong to build up reserves, and beyond what the military governor was allowed to keep he seized all revenue and supplies. The emperor therefore hated him.

sentences.zh: 壬午，百官入見，獨收延朗付御史台，餘皆謝恩。

translations.literal: On renwu the officials entered audience; Yanlang alone was seized and handed over to the Censorate — all the rest expressed gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the officials entered audience. Yanlang alone was seized and handed over to the Censorate, while all the rest expressed their gratitude.

sentences.zh: 甲申，車駕入宮，大赦：「應中外官吏一切不問，惟賊臣張延朗、劉延皓、劉延朗奸邪貪猥，罪難容貸；

translations.literal: On jiashen the imperial carriage entered the palace and issued a grand amnesty: "All officials within and without shall be questioned on nothing — only the treacherous ministers Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, and Liu Yanlang, wicked, greedy, and base, whose crimes cannot be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the imperial carriage entered the palace and issued a grand amnesty: "All officials within and without shall be questioned on nothing — only the treacherous ministers Zhang Yanlang, Liu Yanhao, and Liu Yanlang, wicked, greedy, and base, whose crimes cannot be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、平章事馬胤孫、樞密使房暠、宣徽使李專美、河中節度使韓昭胤等，雖居重位，不務詭隨，並釋罪除名；

translations.literal: Secretariat vice director and chief minister Ma Yinsun, Privy Council commissioner Fang Hao, Palace Directorate commissioner Li Zhuanmei, Hezhong military governor Han Zhaoyin, and others, though they held high rank, did not practice deceitful compliance — all are released from guilt and removed from office;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat vice director and chief minister Ma Yinsun, Privy Council commissioner Fang Hao, Palace Directorate commissioner Li Zhuanmei, Hezhong military governor Han Zhaoyin, and others, though they held high rank, did not practice deceitful compliance — all are released from guilt and removed from office;

sentences.zh: 中外臣僚先歸順者，委中書門下別加任使。」

translations.literal: officials within and without who submitted first shall be entrusted to the Secretariat and Chancellery for separate appointment."
translations.idiomatic: officials within and without who submitted first shall be entrusted to the Secretariat and Chancellery for separate appointment."

sentences.zh: 劉延皓匿於成門，數日，自經死。

translations.literal: Liu Yanhao hid at Chen Gate; after several days he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanhao hid at Chen Gate. After several days he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 劉延朗將奔南山，捕得，殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang was about to flee to South Mountain; captured, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang was about to flee to South Mountain. Captured, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 斬張延朗；

translations.literal: Zhang Yanlang was beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanlang was beheaded;

sentences.zh: 既而選三司使，難其人，帝甚悔之。

translations.literal: Later, when choosing a Three Commissions director, no suitable man could be found, and the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when choosing a Three Commissions director, no suitable man could be found, and the emperor deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 閩人聞唐主之亡，歎曰：「潞王之罪，天下未之聞也，將如吾君何！」

translations.literal: When the people of Min heard of the Tang ruler's death, they sighed: "The Prince of Lu's crime — the realm has not heard of it. What will become of our lord!"
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Min heard of the Tang ruler's death, they sighed, "The Prince of Lu's crime — the realm has not heard of it. What will become of our lord!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉朔，帝如河陽，餞太相溫及契丹兵歸國。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day yiyou, the emperor went to Heyang to give a farewell banquet for Grand Chancellor Wen and the Khitan troops returning to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day yiyou, the emperor went to Heyang to give a farewell banquet for Grand Chancellor Wen and the Khitan troops returning home.

sentences.zh: 追廢唐主為庶人。

translations.literal: The Tang emperor was posthumously deposed and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor was posthumously deposed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以馮道兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dinghai Feng Dao was additionally made vice director of the Chancellery and chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Feng Dao was additionally made vice director of the Chancellery and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 曹州刺史鄭阮貪暴，指揮使石重立因亂殺之，族其家。

translations.literal: Cao Prefecture prefect Zheng Ruan was greedy and cruel; commander Shi Chongli took advantage of the chaos to kill him and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Prefecture prefect Zheng Ruan was greedy and cruel. Commander Shi Chongli took advantage of the chaos to kill him and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以唐中書侍郎姚顗為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On xinmao Tang Secretariat vice director Yao Yi was made vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Tang Secretariat vice director Yao Yi was made vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初，朔方節度使張希崇為政有威信，民夷愛之，興屯田以省漕運；

translations.literal: Earlier, Shuofang military governor Zhang Xichong governed with authority and trust; Han and non-Han alike loved him. He established military colonies to economize on transport by canal;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shuofang military governor Zhang Xichong governed with authority and trust, and Han and non-Han alike loved him. He established military colonies to economize on canal transport;

sentences.zh: 在鎮五年，求內徙，唐潞王以為靜難節度使。

translations.literal: after five years in the command he sought transfer inward; the Tang Prince of Lu made him Jingnan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: after five years in the command he sought transfer inward, and the Tang Prince of Lu made him Jingnan military governor.

sentences.zh: 帝與契丹修好，恐其復取靈武，癸巳，復以希崇為朔方節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor made peace with the Khitan and feared they might retake Lingwu. On guisi he again made Xichong Shuofang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made peace with the Khitan and feared they might retake Lingwu. On guisi he again made Xichong Shuofang military governor.

sentences.zh: 初，成德節度使董溫琪貪暴，積貨巨萬，以牙內都虞侯平山秘瓊為腹心。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chengde military governor Dong Wenqi was greedy and cruel and amassed goods worth tens of thousands. He took intramural deputy chief commander Pingshan Mi Qiong as his trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chengde military governor Dong Wenqi was greedy and cruel and amassed goods worth tens of thousands. He took intramural deputy chief commander Pingshan Mi Qiong as his trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 溫琪與趙德鈞俱沒於契丹，瓊盡殺溫琪家人，瘞於一坎，而取其貨，自稱留後，表稱軍亂。

translations.literal: Wenqi perished in Khitan hands together with Zhao Dejun. Qiong killed all of Wenqi's family, buried them in a single pit, seized his goods, declared himself acting governor, and memorialized that there had been a military mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqi perished in Khitan hands together with Zhao Dejun. Qiong killed all of Wenqi's family, buried them in a single pit, seized his goods, declared himself acting governor, and memorialized that there had been a military mutiny.

sentences.zh: 同州小校門鐸殺節度使楊漢賓，焚掠州城。

translations.literal: Tong Prefecture junior officer Men Duo killed military governor Yang Hanbin and burned and plundered the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Prefecture junior officer Men Duo killed military governor Yang Hanbin and burned and plundered the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 詔贈李贊華燕王，遣使送其喪歸國。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Li Zanhua as Prince of Yan and sent an envoy to escort his coffin back to his homeland.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Li Zanhua as Prince of Yan and sent an envoy to return his coffin to Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 張朗將其眾入朝。

translations.literal: Zhang Lang led his troops to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang led his troops to present themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以唐中書侍郎、同平章事盧文紀為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Lu Wenji of Tang, vice director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was made minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Lu Wenji of Tang, former vice director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was appointed minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以皇城使晉陽周瑰為大將軍、充三司使；

translations.literal: Zhou Gui of Jinyang, imperial city commissioner, was made grand general and acting commissioner of the Three Commissions;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Gui of Jinyang, imperial city commissioner, was made grand general and acting commissioner of the Three Commissions;

sentences.zh: 瑰辭曰：「臣自知才不稱職，寧以避事見棄，猶勝冒寵獲辜。」

translations.literal: Gui declined, saying: "This subject knows his talent does not match the post. Better to be cast aside for avoiding duty than to accept favor and incur guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Gui declined, saying, "I know my talent does not match the post. I would rather be cast aside for shirking duty than accept favor and incur guilt."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝聞平盧節度使房知溫卒，遣天平節度使王建立將兵巡撫青州。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Fang Zhiwen, military governor of Pinglu, had died and sent Wang Jianli, military governor of Tianping, with troops to pacify Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Fang Zhiwen, military governor of Pinglu, had died, he sent Wang Jianli, military governor of Tianping, with troops to pacify Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 改興唐府曰廣晉府。

translations.literal: The Xingtang Prefecture was renamed Guangjin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xingtang Prefecture was renamed Guangjin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安遠節度使盧文進聞帝為契丹所立，自以本契丹叛將，辛丑，棄鎮奔吳。

translations.literal: Lu Wenjin, military governor of Anyuan, heard the emperor had been installed by the Khitan. Considering himself originally a Khitan defector, on xinchou he abandoned his command and fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenjin, military governor of Anyuan, heard the emperor had been installed by the Khitan. As a former Khitan defector himself, on xinchou he abandoned his post and fled to Wu.

sentences.zh: 所過鎮戍，召其主將，告之故，皆拜辭而退。

translations.literal: At every garrison he passed, he summoned its commander, told him the reason, and all bowed, took leave, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At every garrison he passed, he summoned the commander, explained his reasons, and each bowed, took leave, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥以荊南節度使、太尉兼中書令李德誠、德勝節度使兼中書令周本位望隆重，欲使之帥眾推戴，本曰：「我受先王大恩，自徐溫父子用事，恨不能救楊氏之危，又使我為此，可乎！」

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao, because Li Decheng, military governor of Jingnan, Grand Marshal and concurrently director of the Secretariat, and Zhou Ben, military governor of Desheng and concurrently director of the Secretariat, were men of weighty standing, wished them to lead the masses in urging his elevation. Ben said: "I received great favor from the former king. Since the Xu Wen father and son held power, I have regretted that I could not save the Yang house in its peril — and now you would have me do this. How can that be fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao wished Li Decheng, military governor of Jingnan, Grand Marshal and concurrently director of the Secretariat, and Zhou Ben, military governor of Desheng and concurrently director of the Secretariat — both men of great standing — to lead the court in urging his elevation. Ben said, "I received great favor from the former king. Since the Xu Wen father and son held power, I have regretted that I could not save the Yang house in its peril. And now you would have me do this. How can that be fitting!"

sentences.zh: 其子弘祚強之，不得已與德誠帥諸將詣江都表吳主，陳知誥功德，請行冊命；

translations.literal: His son Hongzuo pressed him; unable to refuse, he joined Decheng in leading the generals to Jiangdu to memorialize the Wu ruler, set forth Zhigao's merits, and request the conferral of the imperial mandate;
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongzuo pressed him until he could not refuse. He joined Decheng in leading the generals to Jiangdu to memorialize the Wu ruler, set forth Zhigao's merits, and request investiture;

sentences.zh: 又詣金陵勸進。

translations.literal: they also went to Jinling to urge his advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: they also went to Jinling to urge Zhigao to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘謂德誠之子建勳曰：「尊公，太祖元勳，今日掃地矣。」

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu said to Decheng's son Jianxun: "Your honored father, a founding meritocrat of the Taizu, is today swept to the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu said to Decheng's son Jianxun, "Your honored father, a founding meritocrat of the Taizu, is today brought low."

sentences.zh: 於是吳宮多妖，吳主曰：「吳祚其終乎！」

translations.literal: Thereupon many portents appeared in the Wu palace. The Wu ruler said: "Is the Wu mandate at its end!"
translations.idiomatic: Many portents then appeared in the Wu palace. The Wu ruler said, "Is the fate of Wu at its end!"

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「此乃天意，非人事也。」

translations.literal: Those at his side said: "This is Heaven's intent, not human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side said, "This is Heaven's intent, not human affairs."

sentences.zh: 高麗王建用兵擊破新羅、百濟，於是東夷諸國皆附之，有二京、六府、九節度、百二十郡。

translations.literal: Wang Jian of Goryeo used troops to defeat Silla and Baekje, whereupon all the eastern Yi states attached themselves to him. He had two capitals, six prefectures, nine military commissions, and one hundred twenty commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of Goryeo used troops to defeat Silla and Baekje, whereupon all the eastern Yi states submitted to him. His realm had two capitals, six prefectures, nine military commissions, and one hundred twenty commanderies.
